resolution.text: A definition embedded in the entity that uses it (a unit's own rule, a hero upgrade) wins over the same term in data.keywords; Battle Companies definitions win over the vanilla file, which is only a reference store and is never modified. A vanilla name defined more than once is resolved by the first occurrence unless data.vanillaAmbiguities pins another one.

validations.message: A Battle Company may have up to 15 members (12 for Elite companies; some companies allow more).
A Battle Company has a maximum of one Leader.
A Battle Company has a maximum of two Sergeants. Other Heroes are Heroes in the Making.
Each Hero may only ever have a single Creature, attached to the Leader or a Sergeant (max. 3 per company).
A Battle Company may only ever have one Wanderer at a time.

validations.name: Path of the Sorcerer
validations.message: Path of the Sorcerer (0 - 1): rare limit of 1 per company.
A model may only carry one Large and one Small piece of Equipment (a Backpack adds three more Small pieces).

text.heroes: When you start a Battle Company you select three of its members to become Heroes; they each get a single point of Might, Will and Fate and are treated as Hero models (all are Minor Heroes). One is the Leader (and may use Last Stand!), the other two are Sergeants. The rest are Heroes in the Making.
text.heroicActions: New Hero models can only use the universal Heroic Actions (Move, Shoot, Combat) and the special Heroic Action of their Path (if applicable) when they start.
text.gold: Some factions indicate a number of Gold in the Starting Company. Gold may be spent in the Equipment & Creatures section of the Armoury: treat the initial Rating of the Equipment, Creature or Wanderer as its Gold value and ignore the Influence cost. Alternatively, Gold can buy additional Wargear for starting models as long as Warriors stay legal to one of their profile's Options.
text.customSelection: At the discretion of the Campaign Organiser, a starting roster may be built from models anywhere in the company's charts and tables. It may not exceed 60 points, including wargear, equipment and creatures, and must adhere to any restrictions.
text.choiceOfOptions: A 'Choice of Options' result lets the model take any option on its profile, except any Option that features a Banner, Warhorn or War Drum.
text.companyHeroUpgrade: Any Hero may replace a result from their Path with their company's Company Hero Upgrade, if they do not already have it.
text.companySpecialRules: A Company Special Rule is a modifier that automatically applies to the models detailed on the company page, at no additional rating.
text.onTheirOwnPath: Models that are On Their Own Path may not gain Experience or receive any kind of Advancement or Promotion.
text.wargears: Models in a Battle Company cannot swap wargear between each other. A Warrior may drop wargear if it translates to another Option of its standard profile (marking down the difference in rating). Heroes can freely drop any wargear from their Options.
text.youDontHaveMySword: Optional: Heroes may discard any Wargear, even if it is built into the base profile. Any armour is discarded, not downgraded. This does not impact the model's rating unless the group decides otherwise.

good.text: Today I take command of this Battle Company to stand against the Shadow. Henceforth let it be called {name}, and may our deeds bring hope to everyone who looks to us.

evil.text: Today I take command of this warband in the name of the Dark Lord. Henceforth let it be called {name}, and let our enemies learn to dread it.

Each enemy Hero or Monster they slay
Preventing a Wound by spending a Fate point
Rolling for and then passing a Courage test for being Broken
Carrying or being within range of an Objective at the end of the game (includes escaping off the board edge, controlling sections of the board, etc.)

notes: If the rider of a Cavalry model is slain but their mount stays on the board, any wounds dealt by the mount still grant Experience Points to the model.
Wargs: some companies feature Wild or Fell Warg Warriors that may promote to a warg ridden by an Orc. The rider assumes the identity of the model - the Warg has been successfully tamed!
Bonus Progression Rolls: some Scenarios offer 'free' advancements for a great feat or mission objective. They are not counted against the amount a model should have for its Experience Points.

injuries.applies: Every model removed as a casualty (except models that fled the board) rolls on the chart for its type. Models that are Injured do not count towards the company's Rating.

rollModifier.text: A modifier (Healing Herbs +1) is added to the 2d6 total before the chart is read; a total above 12 reads as 12.

warrior.name: Dead
warrior.text: Remove the Warrior, and all their wargear, from the Company Roster.

warrior.name: Injured
warrior.text: The Warrior must miss the next game that your Battle Company participates in, but suffers no further effects.

warrior.name: Full Recovery
warrior.text: The Warrior makes a full recovery, and may fight in the next battle as normal.

warrior.name: Lesson Learned
warrior.text: The Warrior is considered to have made a Full Recovery. Additionally, the Warrior gains +D3 Experience.

hero.name: Dead
hero.text: Your Hero's adventure ends here; no doubt their followers will mourn them. Remove the Hero, and all of their wargear, from your Battle Company Roster.

hero.name: Arm Wound
hero.text: From this point on, the Hero cannot benefit from a shield in any way, use a two-handed weapon, pike, or fire a bow or crossbow of any sort. They may still carry a Company Standard with the normal penalties and fight with a Hand Weapon. If the Hero would suffer a second Arm Wound, they will be forced to retire, as per the Dead result.

hero.name: Leg Wound
hero.text: The Hero has their Move value permanently reduced by 1". If the Hero would suffer a second Leg Wound, they will be forced to retire, as per the Dead result.

hero.name: Broken Honour
hero.text: The Hero has been shamed in battle, they may no longer provide a "Stand Fast!". Nor may they affect members of the Battle Company with their Heroic Actions. Should the Hero suffer this result a second time, they will gain the Fearful special rule. If the Hero would suffer a third Broken Honour, they will be forced to retire, as per the Dead result.

hero.name: T'is Just a Scratch
hero.text: They must miss the next game. Alternatively, the Hero may roll again on this chart - however, the second result will apply even if it is worse than the first. If this result should occur after any reroll, the Hero must miss the next game.

hero.name: Full Recovery
hero.text: The Hero may play in the next game as normal. Additionally, the Hero may heal one Arm Wound, Leg Wound, or Broken Honour they previously obtained. This resets the "count" that the specific Injury is giving them toward a forced retirement.

hero.name: Protection by the Valar
hero.text: The Hero is considered to have made a Full Recovery. Additionally, the Hero permanently gains +1 Fate point (to their Path's Maximum).

hero.name: Wounds of a Hero
hero.text: The Hero model's Battle Company immediately gains an extra D6 Influence Points; additionally, the Hero is considered to have made a Full Recovery.

retirement.text: A Hero that would suffer a retireAtCount-th occurrence of an injury is forced to retire, as per the Dead result: removed from the roster with all wargear.

injuries.deathOfAHero: If your Leader is slain, choose one of your Sergeants to be promoted to Leader after the battle. If you ever have less than two Sergeants, another Hero who is not already a Leader or Sergeant may become a Sergeant. If there is no Hero available, the Warrior with the most Experience Points is instantly treated as having rolled Hero in the Making on the Warrior Progression Chart (gaining Might, Will and Fate). Ties go to the highest Rating, then the controlling player.

healing.warrior: Spend 1 Influence to remove the Injured condition from a Warrior.
healing.hero: Spend 1 Influence to attempt to remove an Injury from a Hero on a 5+ (the roll may be modified with additional Influence the same way as a Might point), or send the Hero to the healers: they miss the next game but remove one Injury from their profile.

warrior.text: Remove the Injured condition from a Warrior.

hero.text: Spend 1 Influence and roll a D6: on a 5+ remove one Injury, or the miss-next-game status of T'is Just a Scratch (the Hero then plays the next game). The roll may be raised with additional Influence, as with a Might point. A failed attempt loses the Influence; the player may try again, with no limit.
Send the Hero to the healers: no roll, the Hero misses the next game but removes one Injury.

xp.bonusRolls: scenario description, not counted against experience
xp.text: Experience is a running total and is never spent or lost: a model has earned floor(XP / 5) rolls, takes them one by one (several can be waiting) and keeps its Experience Points when it is promoted or becomes a Hero.

timing.text: Progression is step 3 of the War's Aftermath, after injuries and experience and before influence. There is no rule for rolling at another time.

progression.rerollSource: campaign.againstTheOdds.bonuses[key=reroll] (a re-roll of the War's Aftermath for a single result)

table.name: No Change
table.text: The Warrior does not gain a promotion.

table.name: Promoted
table.text: The Warrior has been granted a promotion by the leader of the company. Check the Advancements table on the company's page: the Warrior exchanges all characteristics and wargear for the new profile, while retaining any wargear that the new profile allows. A Warrior eligible for several promotions picks one. If there is no promotion, the Warrior increases Courage & Intelligence by +1 each, to a maximum of 3+.

table.name: A Hero in the Making
table.text: The Warrior is treated as a Hero and immediately gains 1 Might, Will, and Fate point. They retain their Experience Points and advance like a Hero from the next game on. Alternatively the model may forgo the Hero's Journey and take their Promotion instead.

hero.pathSelection: All Heroes select their Path the moment they become a Hero, either via Company Creation or Warrior Progression, and gain any starting rules and abilities related to their Path.
hero.text: Each time a Hero gains 5 Experience Points they roll two pairs of six-sided dice (2d6), note the sum of each pair, and choose one of the two results. The Hero may only roll on their chosen Path, unless an Advancement, special rule or Scenario bonus says otherwise.

rollAgain.meaning: also take the other pair's result

resolution.optionsAre: alternatives: when a row has several options (or a oneOf) the player chooses one
resolution.ratingEffect: an increase adds rating only above campaign.characteristicLimits.average (campaign.rating.hero.perPoint)

hero.unavailableResults: If neither result can be gained due to Characteristic Maximums or duplicate Special Rules, re-roll any unavailable results until an applicable result is found (if possible).
hero.companyHeroUpgradeSwap: Regardless of availability, a Hero may swap any result for their Company Specific Hero Upgrade if they don't already have it.
hero.exhausted: If a Hero has already exhausted every possible result on their path, they have learned all that they need to know.
hero.pathResultTemplate: Rolls 2, 3, 7, 11 and 12 are Path-specific; 4: Attacks or Wounds +1; 5: Courage or Intelligence +1 (and take the other roll too); 6: Strength or Defence +1; 8: Fight or Shoot +1; 9: Might, Will or Fate +1; 10: Minor Special Rule or a new Heroic Action.

limitKinds.max: highest value the stat may reach
limitKinds.maxIncrease: most the stat may be raised above the profile it started with
limitKinds.best: best (lowest) value allowed, for the stats where lower is better

average.text: The profile of an Average Battle Company character. Advancements that bring a Hero's characteristic to equal or under these values do not add to the Hero's rating.

peak.text: The peak of a Battle Company character's growth: the overall ceiling for each characteristic. Each Heroic Path has its own, lower limits. Once at a maximum a Hero may not increase it again, but may still gain temporary bonuses from special rules or wargear.

influence.text: A Battle Company always gains 2 Influence Points for participating in a Scenario, +1 for a Draw and +2 for a Win.
influence.allIsLost: Any Battle Company may voluntarily flee the battlefield once their force is Broken, decided at the beginning of the turn they are broken and before priority. The opponent claims victory and full scenario rewards; the fleeing company earns the standard Influence for participating, but nothing further.

spend.name: Recruit Reinforcements
spend.text: Roll on the company's Reinforcement chart. It costs 3 Influence for most companies (see each company page for its Reinforcement cost). A Special Chart result lets you continue on the company's Special Chart. If a roll would give a Rare model the company cannot have, choose a lower result on the same chart. If a roll would break the Wargear Limits you may either increase your roll with Influence or take the next option down.

spend.name: Adjust a Reinforcement Roll
spend.text: For each Influence Point spent you may increase the die of a Reinforcement roll by 1 (house rule: the rulebook also allows decreasing; lowering is never paid, see campaign.recruitment). Spent Influence does not carry over to adjust rolls on the Special Chart. A maximum of 3 Influence can be spent adjusting across both the regular and Special Charts per Reinforcement Roll.

spend.name: Treat Injuries
spend.text: Spend 1 Influence to: remove the Injured condition from a Warrior; attempt to remove an Injury from a Hero on a 5+ (modifiable with additional Influence like a Might point); or send a Hero to the healers (they miss the next game but remove one Injury).

spend.name: Visit the Armoury
spend.text: Buy additional equipment and wargear for the cost in Influence Points. Warriors may only buy wargear matching one of their profile's Options. Heroes may take any wargear (including Armour upgrades) available to any profile included in their company's Reinforcement and Special Charts and Promotion table.

influence.reinforcementRollOfOne: Nobody steps forward: no Influence is spent but you may not roll again this Post-Battle Sequence.
influence.rareUnits: Models shown with (Rare X) can only ever be taken up to X times by a company.
influence.specialUnits: Some companies have profiles that are not on their charts (e.g. Moria's Cave Troll). They have their own costs and limitations on the company page.
influence.wargearLimits: Battle Companies use the MESBG Bow & Throwing limits, but Heroes count towards them. Additionally, only up to 33% of a Battle Company may have the Cavalry keyword. Promotions are affected by these limits. Some companies list exceptions.

rating.text: The Battle Company Rating is the sum of the rating of its models. Models that are missing the next game because they are Injured do not count.
rating.warrior: A Warrior is worth the same points as in MESBG plus the rating of any Equipment it bears.

notes: Add the point value of the Warrior profile the Hero is built from, then the ratings above.
Advancements that bring a characteristic to equal or under the Average Battle Company profile (see characteristicLimits.average) do not add to rating.
Special Rules that improve with additional results do not increase in rating with each additional improvement.

wargear.text: Wargear built into the base profile or in the profile's Options list adds no rating. If a Hero's Attacks and Wounds add up to at least 3, wargear and equipment that were neither part of the base profile nor of its Options list use the (hero) rating from the Armoury and Equipment lists. E.g. a Ranger of Gondor pays nothing for armour, bow or spear, but pays for a horse or heavy armour.

againstTheOdds.text: The Battle Company with the lower rating may select Against the Odds bonuses after the roll on the Scenario Table was made, but before setting up. Each bonus adds its Rating to the company's rating, which must not exceed the opponent's as a result of these bonuses. The rating difference is checked before Against the Odds bonuses.

eligible.text: Only the company with the lower Rating chooses; at equal Ratings nobody does. The comparison (and the 25 rating difference of the scenarios with an Attacker and a Defender) is made before Against the Odds bonuses.

budget.text: The sum of the Ratings of the chosen bonuses may not take the lower company above its opponent's Rating (equal is allowed: 'must not exceed'). So a bonus needs a Rating gap at least as large as its price: Ambush! needs a gap of 60 on its own.

defaultNotConfirmed: repeatability of the bonuses other than the Tool Kit

bonuses.name: Influence
bonuses.text: +2 Influence for Victory, +1 for Draw or Defeat.

bonuses.name: Experience
bonuses.text: +2 Experience per model for Victory, +1 per model for Draw or Defeat.

bonuses.name: Reroll
bonuses.text: Two rerolls that each can be used at any point during the game to re-roll a single die or the War's Aftermath for a single result.

bonuses.name: Tool Kit
bonuses.text: You may only have one of each Kit, but their items may be distributed to any members and ignore all capacity / alignment rules.

bonuses.name: Wanderer
bonuses.text: You may temporarily recruit a Wanderer for the match.

grants.rules: data.wanderers.rules (no Stand Fast, no Heroic Actions on the company, no Experience or Advancements)

scenarioSelection.text: Compare the Battle Company Ratings: the higher rating is the Top Dog, the other the Underdog. The Underdog is referenced in scenarios for special rules and automatically wins the roll-off to determine Layout and Starting Positions (on a tie follow the normal scenario rules). Then roll a D6 to pick one of the three tables, and a second D6 to pick the Scenario (ideally rolled by different players).
scenarioSelection.layout: All scenarios are written with a 48"x48" board in mind (36"x36" is popular). Cover the board with a dense amount of terrain; some scenarios have specific terrain requirements.

maelstromOfBattle.text: At the end of each of your Move phases, roll a D6 for one of your models not already on the battlefield and consult the chart (Hero models can use Might to increase this roll), then roll for the next. Models can't Charge in the turn that they arrive. Models yet to arrive count as being on the battlefield for the purposes of determining if your force is Broken.

table.text: The model has not arrived yet.
The model enters the battlefield from the western board edge.
The model enters the battlefield from the eastern board edge.
The model enters the battlefield from the southern board edge.
The model enters the battlefield from the northern board edge.
The model enters the battlefield from any board edge chosen by the controlling player.

specialRules.name: Command Support
specialRules.definition: Units with the Command keyword are referenced periodically in scenarios. This keyword is granted by certain Equipment to represent the command retinue that accompanies the Leader.

specialRules.name: Neutral Third-Party
specialRules.definition: If the NPC Scenario is using the rules for a Neutral Third-Party, there are three sides of the battle: each battle company and the non-player forces. The non-player models activate first in each Move phase, even before Heroic Moves, in the order that is most advantageous to them (e.g. so as not to block each other's paths). What the models do when they activate depends on their behaviour. Regardless of behaviour, neutral models will not take Courage tests for being Broken.

specialRules.name: Aggressive
specialRules.definition: When activated, each model will follow the most efficient path in an effort to Engage models from either Battle Company.

specialRules.name: Passive
specialRules.definition: These models will always Activate first in each Move phase, even before Heroic Move. Starting with the player without Priority, players alternate moving these models until all have been moved. Passive Neutral models do not make any actions that would result in risking failed climb, leap or swim tests. They cannot willingly go prone and will stand up as soon as it is possible. Any neutral model armed with a ranged weapon activates in such a way that they can still shoot. During the Shoot Phase, they must target the nearest enemy model to them that also provides the greatest odds of hitting their target.

specialRules.name: Resolving Combat
specialRules.definition: In a combat involving a neutral model and members of both companies that are not in base contact with one another, strikes will alternate starting with the Company that rolled the highest to win the Duel. Ties in the highest roll are then determined by the highest Fight Value on each side. Further ties are determined by a roll-off. If only one side is engaged with a neutral model, then the opposing player makes all decisions for that model, including using any Brutal Power Attacks! In the event all sides are engaged with each other, then for each combat of this nature the decisions of the NPC in each similar combat will alternate between players; starting with the player without Priority.

specialRules.name: Allies of Convenience
specialRules.definition: Some scenarios pit the Battle Companies against a common enemy. Members of both count as friendly models to each other. Players roll for Priority as normal, with the player that won Priority acting with their models first in each phase if able. When resolving Ranged Attacks or Magical Powers, Good models only follow their Good targeting restrictions if they would risk hitting another Good model.

customCompany.text: Optional: to customise a company beyond Custom Selection, talk with the Campaign Organiser about modifying an existing company (starting company, reinforcement/special charts, advancements and the Company Hero Upgrade).
rulesOfThumb: Keep it Simple, Keep it Safe.
Aim to make design choices that favour a theme over an advantage.
Be wary of multi-attack or multi-wound profiles and special rules that grant +1 to Wound.
Consider adding Equipment to profiles before inventing new profiles from scratch (e.g. a Haradrim Warrior with a Small Shield can create a generic light spearman).
Alternatively, allocate Wargear or Characteristic Increases to create new profiles (e.g. an Orc Tracker with 3+ Shoot and an Uruk Bow might make an Orc Sniper).
Your Starting Battle Company should always add up to a total of 60 points of combined Rating and Gold, before Might / Will / Fate.
As cool as it sounds, a Nazgul does not a company make.

sources.note: some scenarios give Gold to the victor; no scenario in the data lists an amount
the Campaign Organiser may grant Gold in a narrative scenario that is not in the rulebook

gold.text: Gold comes from some companies' starting company, from victory rewards of some scenarios and from the organiser's narrative scenarios; it carries over and can be spent in the Armoury later. Spending at company creation:  an Equipment, Creature or Wanderer costs its initial Rating (point value) in Gold and no Influence; Gold can alternatively buy extra Wargear for starting models as long as Warriors stay legal to one of their profile's Options. The starting company is meant to add up to 60 points of Rating plus Gold (before Might / Will / Fate).

aftermathEffects.text: Two re-rolls, each for a single die or a single result of the War's Aftermath.
+2 Influence for a Victory, +1 for a Draw or Defeat.
+2 Experience per model for a Victory, +1 for a Draw or Defeat.
One Hero that took part and was not removed as a casualty may use Healing Herbs (the item is removed): every Injury roll the company makes at the end of the game gets +1. Not cumulative.
A model removed as a casualty that took part may use its Wondrous Cram (the item is removed): it does not roll on the Injury chart and counts as having rolled the Full Recovery result.
The victorious company may apply +1 / -1 to its first Reinforcement roll in the War's Aftermath right after this match.
aftermathEffects.note: The scenario prints 'in the subsequent War's Aftermath'; the user confirmed (2026-10-21) that it is the aftermath right after the match, not the next match's.

aftermathEffects.text: A company that scores all 6 Objective Markers may acquire a free piece of Equipment worth up to 2 Influence.
Each Leader that is not removed from the board earns one additional Experience Point.
A company that scores all Cargo earns 1 bonus Influence.
The winner of the scenario may apply +1 or -1 to the second die result the next time they roll on the Scenario Table, after both dice have been rolled.
The model in possession of the Relic at the end of the game gains the benefit of the Fortify Spirit Magical Power in their next game, even if they have no Will remaining.

breakPoint.text: A company's force is Broken when its casualties exceed its Break Point, checked at the start of every turn; from then on every model must pass a Courage test before it acts. Battle Companies uses the Broken Army rule of the Rules Manual (page 46) with the Break Point set per company (50%, Muster of Isengard 66%).
source: MESBG Rules Manual: Broken Army (46), Stand Fast (47), Cavalry and Break Points
Battle Companies: All is Lost!, Muster of Isengard company rule, scenario special rules

threshold.text: Break Point = percent of the models that started the game, not rounded (13 models: 6.5; 12 models: 6). Broken when the casualties are greater than the Break Point: exactly 50% lost is not Broken.

startingModels.text: Every model of the company in the starting force, Heroes and Warriors alike; creatures are models on the board and count unless a scenario says otherwise (the Baggage Ponies). Models that arrive later (Maelstrom of Battle) count as being on the battlefield. A Cavalry model is one model; a Chariot is one model; a War Beast and its Commander are two.

casualties.cavalry: The rider's death is the casualty, whether the mount stays or flees; the mount's death alone is not a casualty.
casualties.text: Casualties are the models removed from the board as casualties, including models that flee after failing a Courage test for being Broken.

courageTest.text: Each model of a Broken company takes a Courage test every time it activates, before doing anything else. Models that cannot activate (Engaged in Combat, held by a rule or power) do not test.

standFast.text: A Hero that passes the test calls Stand Fast at the end of its activation: friendly Warriors that activate within 6" and see it pass automatically. Other Heroes test for themselves.

confirmedByUser: fleeingCompany (participation plus the Against the Odds Influence and Experience bonuses, no Win/Draw Influence, no scenario rewards; user decision mqn.114)
defaultNotConfirmed: decidedAt (only the turn it becomes Broken)
allIsLost.text: At the start of the turn it becomes Broken, before the Priority phase, a company may flee the battlefield: the opponent wins and claims the full scenario rewards; the fleeing company keeps the participation Influence and Experience and its Against the Odds Influence and Experience bonuses, but no Win/Draw Influence and no scenario rewards.

experience.text: +1 Experience to each model that rolled for the Courage test for being Broken and passed it, once per match however many times it passed. An automatic pass (Stand Fast, Heroic Resolve, a scenario rule) is not a roll. A model that fails flees and is removed.

scenarioExceptions.text: Models standing on the hill never take Courage tests for being Broken.
Defender models within 6" of the Gate pass every Courage test automatically.
The Defender's Baggage Ponies are not counted when working out its Break Point.
Neutral models never take Courage tests for being Broken.
Models that have not arrived yet count as being on the battlefield when checking whether the company is Broken.

liveMatch.text: The live match shows the starting models, the casualties and the Break Point per company, flags Broken at the start of the turn the test above turns true, and offers All is Lost in that turn.

matchInput.text: Per match the players enter, for each company: the roles, the Against the Odds bonuses, the Victory Points (from the scenario's scoringObjectives), whether the Battle Company fled, the scenario reward flags and, for every model, what happened to it and which experience gains it earned. The winner is the company with the most Victory Points; equal Victory Points are a draw (stated in the Objectives of most scenarios).

perCompany.text: Attacker or Defender, for the scenarios that have roles.
The Against the Odds bonuses taken before setting up; they only apply to the lower rated company (campaign.aftermathEffects).
The total of the Victory Points scored; entered as a total or built up objective by objective.
One entry per scoring objective (tier, count or per-item tiers); 'side' limits an objective to the Attacker or the Defender.
The tickable conditions of the scenario rewards (companyFlag, modelFlag); the conditions victory and leaderNotRemoved are derived from the result and the model outcomes.
The Kits taken (one Tool Kit bonus each, no Kit twice); their items are then assigned to models.
The Wanderer that joins the company for this match only.
The scenario chosen with Ambush!, replacing the rolled one.
Models in the starting force (roster of the match, creatures, temporary Wanderer); the Break Point follows from it.
The turn at whose start the company became Broken, if it did.

All is Lost: the Broken company fled the battlefield; the opponent claims victory and full scenario rewards, the fleeing company keeps the participation Influence and Experience and its Against the Odds Influence and Experience bonuses, but no Win/Draw Influence and no scenario rewards.

perModel.text: A model removed as a casualty rolls on its Injury chart; a model that fled the board does not (campaign.injuries.applies). 'survived' covers every model still on the board at the end.
Every model that took part in the scenario; a model missing the game (Injured) is not in the match roster.
The item the model elects to use before the injury rolls (Healing Herbs: a Hero that was not a casualty; Wondrous Cram: a casualty); it is removed from the Equipment.

aftermath.rewards: campaign.aftermathEffects[] whose key is listed in the scenario's rewards[].effect, applied when its condition holds

gold.text: No scenario of the rulebook rewards Gold; Gold comes from the starting company and from the organiser (campaign.gold.sources).

adjust.text: Influence raises the DIE, one point per Influence, at most 3 per recruiting attempt across the reinforcement chart and the special chart together. A 5 raised by 1 becomes a 6 and leads on to the special chart. If the rolled result and the next ones cannot be recruited, the player still pays for every point needed to reach the result they want. Lowering is never paid.

rare.text: A unit marked Rare N can be in the company at most N times at the same time: the units of that profile currently in the roster. Injured units count; units that died, left, or were promoted into another profile no longer count. When a roll gives a rare unit the company cannot have, it cannot be recruited and the player takes a lower result (lowerResult, reason rareExhausted).

unitChoice.semantics: The player picks ONE option whose own rare limit is not exhausted (the company has fewer than `rare` of that profile). If every option is exhausted the result cannot be recruited and the normal lowerResult rule applies on the same chart.
unitChoice.text: A chart row that offers a choice among named units, each with its own Rare limit.

lowerResult.text: When the rolled result cannot be recruited (rare units used up, over the model maximum, over a keyword or wargear limit, a race balance) or a company rule says so, the player may take ANY lower result for free. A lower result may not be picked just because the player prefers it. A company effect (recruitFallback) can widen the scope, e.g. to both charts.

options.label: Heroes may discard any wargear
options.description: Heroes may drop wargear that is part of their profile.

options.label: Path of Their Own Making (homebrew)
options.description: Units that are On Their Own Path level up on a homebrew path instead of staying warriors.

options.label: Shake the table
options.description: Throw the 3D dice with physics: one shake per roll.

options.label: Players may enter their own rolls
options.description: Let players type in the result of a roll instead of rolling in the app.

companies.name: Minas Tirith
companies.description:
Known as the Tower of the Guard, the mighty walled city of Minas Tirith is the bulwark that has kept the endless legions of the Red Eye at bay through the long and gruelling centuries. Mighty though her ramparts are, the defenders of the White City cannot stand idle behind their fortifications and hope for victory. Instead, at the Steward's orders, warbands and patrols must constantly venture forth, hunting down the spies of Mordor and guarding key locations such as river-crossings and vantage points.

For the warriors of Minas Tirith selected for such duties, great risk and thrilling adventure beckon – success will see promotion, glory and riches, for nothing in the land of Gondor is valued more than the courage and strength required to keep its lands safe.

heroUpgrades.name: The Charge of Gondor
heroUpgrades.flavour: With a rousing cry, the hero plunges themselves into the fray in defence of Minas Tirith.

oath.text: By the white walls of the Tower of Guard I take this company in my charge, to hold the line where the fires of the Enemy burn. Let us be known as {name}, and let Gondor never fall.

companies.name: Osgiliath & Ithilien
companies.description:
The city of Osgiliath has had a varied and turbulent past. Once, it stood tall and proud as the capital of the realm of Gondor; a beacon of hope and valour against the growing threat of Mordor. Over time, it became ravaged by war, eventually falling into ruin. Since those days, it has been the site for many a battle between Gondor and its foes, and in the later years of the Third Age it has been garrisoned by the forces of Gondor as a stronghold.

Often, small groups made up of those stationed within Osgiliath's ruined walls are sent out from the city and into the wilderness. These bands would journey east to the edge of the realm of Gondor in search of invaders. It is not unheard of for these companies to venture even further out to give aid to settlements and allies that are under threat from the forces of Evil.

heroUpgrades.name: Remember Today
heroUpgrades.flavour: The Rangers of Ithilien have mastered ways of communicating that appear to be natural, and use this to plan with one another while lying in ambush.

companies.name: Fiefdoms
companies.description:
Since the days of old, the Fiefdoms of Gondor have been pledged to defend her in times of need. Many of the cities under Gondor's protection host skilled standing armies with warriors prepared to do their duty, yet peace remains out of reach. Packs of Orcs will often attack cities and outposts, intent on bringing death and ruin to their people, and Corsair slave raids are commonplace on the coastlines to the south.

It is because of this that bands of warriors from the major cities of Gondor's Fiefdoms patrol the lands of Gondor to protect the race of Men against the threat of Mordor. Often, an aspiring Swan Knight from Dol Amroth will gather Men from Lossarnach, Lamedon, and Morthond in order to venture forth and quell the threats that stalk their lands.

companies.name: Fornost
companies.description:
At the time when the Kingdom of Arnor was crumbling and embroiled in constant war with the forces of the Witch-king, Arvedui sent messages requesting aid to Gondor, Arnor's sister kingdom in the south. However, Gondor itself was at war with Mordor and its allies to the east and south, and was unable to send aid northwards with as much haste as they would have liked

Yet Gondor will not fight alone against the darkness. Elves gathered the remnants of the people of Arnor that were scattered to the forest of the northern lands; even the Hobbits of the Shire sent a small band of Bounders to join the fight. Together, the combined forces of Men and Elves (and Hobbits) will wage war upon Angmar to avenge the Kingdom of Arnor that now lies in ruins.

heroUpgrades.name: Defiance
heroUpgrades.flavour: Though Arnor has fallen, these brave people will stop at nothing to avenge the kingdom.

companies.name: Arnor
companies.description:
Arnor was once a great realm, formed by Elendil in the Second Age, however, by the dwindling years of the Third Age, Arnor had fallen into ruin; a shadow of its former glory. Yet in days gone by, even as it fell into despair, the Kings of Arnor would send out patrols of their warriors to protect the realm against the swarms of fell creatures under the Witch-king's command.

Those who led these small patrols were warriors who were destined to command Arnor's armies, but did not yet possess the experience required to lead. They would set out from Fornost with their loyal companions to fend off the Orc raiding parties that threatened their home. These warbands were also used by the kings of old to explore the crumbling ruins that were once Arnor's cities, abandoned long ago, in search of heirlooms of their forebears.

heroUpgrades.name: Foresight of the Seer
heroUpgrades.flavour: It is the hero's sworn duty to protect the realm of Arnor, no matter the cost.

specialRules: "Leave all that can be spared behind. We travel light." - As Arnor fell, the Dunedain grew wilder and more dangerous in their vigil.

oath.text: Heirs of Arnor, I take command of this company to keep the watch our kings began, and to carry the fury of the North against the servants of the Witch-king. From this day let us be called {name}. May that name bring dread to our foes and hope to our people.

companies.name: The Last Alliance
companies.description:
In the closing years of the Second Age, the armies of Gil-galad and Elendil formed a compact that would become known as the Last Alliance of Men and Elves, to combat the ever-growing threat of Sauron. Marching to war upon the black lands of Mordor, they fought for many years against the hordes of Orcs that Sauron sent to oppose them. During these blighted years, it was not unusual for Gil-galad and Elendil to send small bands of their warriors to venture into Mordor to undermine the armies of the Dark Lord.

These companies would be tasked with dealing with enemy scouts before they could give away their army's position, capturing small Orc outposts, or even assassinating leaders of the Orcish armies. As these companies of Men and Elves fought together, the bonds between them grew to a point where they would fight better when alongside their allies than even when alongside those of their own race.

heroUpgrades.name: There Were Some Who Resisted
heroUpgrades.flavour: The alliance forged between Men and Elves has brought out the best in both races as they fight against the Dark Lord.

companies.name: Rohan
companies.description:
Though Rohan is a lush and fertile land of rolling plains and gentle hills, it is a kingdom much used to the cruelty of war. Constant raids from the neighbouring Dunlendings, and a history of battle against foes as varied as Orcs and even the Variags of Khand, have forced the men of the Mark to keep a watchful eye over their domain. Across Rohan, her people gather within the palisades of fortified towns and villages, never straying far from safety.

To ensure that the lands between these settlements are free of invaders, constant patrols march along Rohan's borders and guard her roadways, well-armed and ready to drive back evil-doers. Such a duty might seem ignominious to some, but for those who wish to demonstrate their worth to the Marshals of the Mark, there is no better proving ground. Thus can Rohan's captains find a ready supply of young fighters, full of bravado and the confidence of youth, eager to prove themselves. Those who take up these duties either return as settled, experienced warriors... or they do not return at all.

heroUpgrades.flavour: Should the leadership of the company find themselves unhorsed, the Rohirrim will gladly give up their own mounts to see their leaders ride again.

companies.name: Helm's Deep
companies.description:
The assault upon the Westfold has forced the people of Rohan to flee to the sanctuary of Helm's Deep; the attack on their lands having highlighted their need for greater protection and taller walls. Having journeyed across Rohan, and survived the ambush of the Wolves of Isengard, the Rohirrim have reached Helm's Deep and begin to prepare for the inevitable battle against the armies of the White Wizard.

As the legions of Saruman's fighting Uruk-hai come into view, the heavens open and begin a downpour upon the fortress of Helm's Deep. Théoden stands atop the Hornburg with his trusted guard, ready to command his forces in the coming battle. Upon the Deeping Wall, ranks of Men and Elves stand side-by-side with one another, honouring the allegiance that stood between Elendil and Gil-galad over three thousand years ago.

Having decided to answer Gondor's call for aid, Théoden led as many men as he could muster as they rode to the White City to face the might of Mordor head-on. Yet the road to Minas Tirith is long and fraught with danger, and so the venerable king sent advance parties with trusted members of Ghân-buri-Ghân's Woses Warriors to assist them.

The combined forces of these two fierce peoples prove deadly when side-by-side, and using paths that only the Woses now remember, the Rohirrim are able to chase down and fell the Orc-folk even as they try to escape through the Drúadan Forest; for the alliance of Rohan and the Woses has proven to be one that can bring the fight to any that oppose them.

companies.name: Erebor & Dale
companies.description:
To the east of Mirkwood lies the great Dwarven realm of Erebor, once ruled over by Thrór, The Last King Under the Mountain. Over the years, Erebor forged a great alliance with Dale, City of Men, and its lord, Girion. Trade was prevalent between the two peoples, with the Dwarves using Dale's grand markets to trade their wares across Middle-Earth, and in return provide the armouries of Dale with finely-wrought weapons. Yet the greatest asset these allies provided each other was a combined strength-in-arms.

It was commonplace for a small band of Dwarves from Erebor and Men from Dale to be tasked with the defence of an outpost; one that provided great benefits to both realms. Groups such as these often ended up forming close bonds as they honed their skills side-by-side in the wild lands of Middle-earth, sharing both talents and experiences with each other.

heroUpgrades.flavour: Well respected by their people, their presence encourages those around them to fight all the harder.

companies.name: Defenders of the North
companies.description:
Over the years, Erebor has helped in the reconstruction of Dale, City of Men, and the royalty of the two kingdoms have shared a strong bond. Trade was prevalent between the two peoples, with the Dwarves using Dale's grand markets to trade their wares across Middle-Earth, and in return provide the armouries of Dale with finely-wrought weapons. Yet the greatest asset these allies provided each other was a combined strength-in-arms.

As the Shadow in the East grew, the dwarves and men found themselves fighting side by side against the forces of darkness once more. With the ancient Knights of Dale reinstated, Dale has never been stronger than ever to rival their old friend.

heroUpgrades.name: Defender
heroUpgrades.flavour: The friendship forged between the youth of the two kingdoms is a bond that can only be broken in death and neither party is keen on letting that happen.

companies.name: Lothlorien
companies.description:
Home to Galadriel, the Lady of Light, and the Elven ring of Nenya, Lothlórien is well guarded by the Elves who live there. Few are ever permitted to pass through the Golden Wood, but those who are granted this honour are met by the Lord and Lady of Lórien in good spirits. Yet the woodland realm of Lórien has come under threat from Evil in the past, as packs of Orcs, Goblins and other Evil creatures constantly seek to infiltrate its boughs.

It is because of this that the Galadhrim wander the well-trodden paths of Lothlórien, ensuring that they are free of Evil and that peace remains. The Elves who lead these patrols are veterans of Ages past, experienced in ways of combat from the many wars they have fought. It is not unheard of for these Elves to range out into Middle-earth in search of Sauron's forces, intent on seeing the Dark Lord finally vanquished.

heroUpgrades.name: Blessing of the Golden Wood
heroUpgrades.flavour: Through the blessing of Galadriel, fortune smiles upon the hero, keeping them from harm.

uniqueWargear.name: Wood Elf Spear
uniqueWargear.definition: This is an Elven spear. Additionally, a model armed with a Wood Elf Spear may use the Shielding rule even though they do not have a shield. Support: an Infantry model with it that is not Engaged in Combat can assist a friendly model in base contact whose base is the same size or smaller. It adds one dice (its own Fight Value) to that Combat's Duel Roll and, if its side wins, makes one Strike with its own Strength. A Supporting model is not involved in the Combat (cannot be struck). It Supports one Combat per Fight Phase and cannot Support if Prone, unable to Activate, or if it shot that turn. It is a hand weapon when the model is Engaged. Elven weapon: If a model fights with an Elven weapon in a Combat, they will be more likely to win the Duel Roll in the result of a Drawn Combat. In these instances, a Good model armed with an Elven weapon will win the roll-off on a 3+, whilst an Evil model armed with an Elven weapon will win the roll-off on a 1-4. If both sides have an Elven weapon, neither side gains the benefit. Some Missile Weapons may also be classed as Elven weapons; however, the above bonus only applies to Melee Weapons.

companies.name: Rivendell
companies.description:
Located in the hidden valley in the western foothills of The Misty Mountains, Rivendell endures under the protection of Elrond and the Elven ring that he possesses. The power of Vilya has kept Rivendell safe, and made it a place of peace and refuge to all of the Free Peoples of Middle-earth, earning it the name 'The Last Homely House'.

However, even places such as Rivendell need protection from the ever-growing Evil in the Third Age. Under Lord Elrond's orders, Elven captains patrol Rivendell's borders, making sure that they are kept free from foul creatures that would bring destruction upon them. Although rare, it has been known for the Elven patrols from Rivendell to venture further beyond their borders, offering aid to those in need against the forces of Sauron.

heroUpgrades.name: Veteran of the Old Wars
heroUpgrades.flavour: A skilled warrior that has fought in many wars across the ages, this hero strikes fear into the hearts of their foes.

companies.name: Halls of Thranduil
companies.description:
Deep within Mirkwood can be found the halls of the Elvenking, Thranduil. This woodland realm is kept hidden within the forest, away from prying eyes and Evil thoughts. Thranduil cares little for the world beyond his realm and will not waste precious lives in keeping it safe. Yet as the years have gone by, even the Elvenking has come to acknowledge the growing threat that is beginning to rise in the old fortress of Dol Guldur.

More and more frequently, the Elvenking has commanded patrols to go out into Mirkwood and clear out the Evil creatures that lurk in the gloom. For the spiders that once resided solely in Dol Guldur have become more brazen and vicious, creeping further and further north, towards the halls of Thranduil. Those in charge of the Elvenking's patrols are tasked with clearing out these spider nests and protecting Mirkwood from all manner of unwelcome 'guests'.

heroUpgrades.flavour: This hero is a swordsman of consummate skill who few can hope to match should they cross blades with them.

companies.name: Durin's Folk
companies.description:
Within the bones of The Misty Mountains, the Dwarves of Durin's Folk built the Dwarven Kingdom of Khazad-dûm. This underground realm, steeped in history and grandeur, was once home to the greatest of the Dwarven lords of Middle- earth, descendants of the father of the Dwarves himself. But as the Dwarves delved deeper in search of precious metals, they sealed their own fate.

In the days when Khazad-dûm prospered, its kings would send their trusted followers to clear the lower tunnels of the mountain, and these warriors would form a tight bond fighting side-by-side against the vile Goblins that dwelt there. Upon their return, these companies would often venture out into Middle-earth, to the other Dwarven Kingdoms such as Erebor, the Iron Hills or the Blue Mountains, in search of wealth and further adventure.

heroUpgrades.name: The Stubbornness of Dwarves
heroUpgrades.flavour: Dwarves do not back down from a fight, no matter how much the odds are stacked against them.

oath.text: Khazad-dum was our mother and our sorrow, and I would see her halls rise again. With axe and iron I bind this clan under the name {name}, and Durin's line shall not be forgotten.

companies.name: Iron Hills
companies.description:
The Dwarves of the Iron Hills are a stubborn and hardy folk, possessing one of the greatest fighting forces of the Third Age. Unlike the Dwarves of other Kingdoms, those of the Iron Hills are famed more for their accomplishments in war than their skill in forging items of great value. It is this that makes an Iron Hills army a deadly and feared foe, one that the forces of the Dark Lord will not eagerly face in battle.

The Iron Hills Dwarves produce such skilled warriors through the constant battles they wage against the Orcs and Goblins that taint their ancestral lands. Before joining the standing army of the Iron Hills, many Dwarves will spend numerous years roaming the lands of Middle-earth honing their skills and dispatching the forces of Evil they encounter. It is through these expeditions that the Dwarves of the Iron Hills become forever bound by the experiences shared upon their many travels and skirmishes with the forces of the Dark Lord.

heroUpgrades.name: Stubborn Brilliance!
heroUpgrades.flavour: This hero is incredibly stubborn even by the standards of the Dwarves and will not stand for being shown up by their enemies.

companies.name: Lake-town
companies.description:
The fishing settlement of Esgaroth has long lived in the shadows of The Lonely Mountain and the threat that lies within. In recent years, Lake-town has fallen upon hard times, with its people struggling to find enough food and shelter. The Master of Lake-town, however, hoards his wealth within his residence, growing ever richer whilst the common folk struggle to make ends meet. Yet the Master of Lake-town's lust for wealth extends further, beyond the borders of Lake-town and into the wider world.

The Master of Lake-town tasks the more opportunistic of his guard to travel across Middle-earth in search of riches, valuable items and trade deals with other realms – some say it was patrols such as these that founded the deal between the Elvenking and Lake-town for their wine. The guards who set out on these ventures will seldom go alone, gathering with them a band of townsfolk from all walks of life to accompany them, promising them the reward of a better life should they return.

heroUpgrades.name: Moneybags
heroUpgrades.flavour: The Master of Lake-town uses his company leaders to distribute the flow of his money. His guards are ever eager to earn his favour and his coin.

companies.name: Wanderers in the Wild
companies.description:
Middle-earth is filled with those of all races that wander its paths and wild lands for many reasons, and it is not uncommon for a group of such wanderers to find common ground and continue on their journeys together. In fact, groups of Men, Elves, Dwarves, and even Hobbits on rare occasions, have been known to travel together through the various realms of Middle-earth, keeping their purposes to themselves.

Often, such bands of wanderers will be called upon by the free folk to help them against those that seek to cause them harm. Though they owe little allegiance to one another, the bonds formed by travelling together with friends is a strong one, and these wanderers will give their all to protect their companions that they now hold dear.

companies.name: The Shire
companies.description:
The Hobbits that reside within the Shire are a peaceful race, quite content to ignore, and be ignored by, the world of the big folk that lies outside their borders. In fact, to many who live in Middle-earth, Hobbits seem of little or no relevance at all and are not considered as warriors or counted among the wise. Hobbits will seldom leave the boundaries of the four Farthings of the Shire, preferring to stay within the comfort of what and where they know.

Yet, on the rare occasion that their livelihoods are threatened, the Hobbits of the Shire can rally to form a fighting force if needed – though not one that possesses a great martial prowess. There have even been occasions, following threats to their homeland, where small bands of Hobbits have ventured beyond the boundaries of the Shire to protect it from those who seek to bring ruin to their quaint and peaceful lives.

heroUpgrades.name: Of a Party Sort
heroUpgrades.flavour: Filled with merriment and ale, the company's spirits are as high as they can be and many feel they can take on anything life would throw at them.

heroUpgrades.name: Throwing Stones
heroUpgrades.flavour: A well placed stone at short range can cause some serious damage to an unwitting foe.

companies.name: Mordor
companies.description:
Mordor; a barren and desolate land filled with darkness and Evil creatures in the service of Sauron. Nothing good can grow in this vile realm, and those who dwell there are driven by malice and cruelty. In the shadows of this blighted place, packs of Orcs skulk in the dark, their leaders constantly looking for opportunities to improve their standing within Sauron's armies, keeping one eye out for inevitable acts of treachery from their underlings.

When these packs become renowned within the land of Mordor, they are often commanded by the Great Eye to leave the Black Lands to bring devastation upon Middle-earth. These packs will then thieve, raid and murder their way into the favour of Sauron. Often, they will attack the outposts of Gondor, Rohan or even further afield, all the time looking to strengthen the influence of the Dark Lord and wreak as much havoc as they can.

heroUpgrades.name: Orcish Brawler
heroUpgrades.flavour: When fighting against the odds, the hero reveals their most savage nature. Hacking and slashing at their enemy in order to prolong their own life.

oath.text: The Great Eye commands, and I obey, for the strong rule and the weak are food. These blades shall be called {name}, and every land that remembers peace shall know the weight of our boots.

companies.name: Cirith Ungol
companies.description:
To the west of Mordor is Cirith Ungol, a fortress that guards the pass that runs through the mountains between Mordor and Gondor. This tall and imposing structure is garrisoned by a rabble of Orcs and Mordor Uruk-hai, two factions that constantly bicker with each other over who truly commands the forces stationed within the tower. They are the first line of defence against whatever should come through the pass, whether that be Elves, Men or something more sinister.

Under the orders of the commanders of the tower, bands of Orcs and Uruk-hai are sent into the pass to patrol its borders in search of anyone brave (or foolish) enough to attempt to cross it, knowing full well that they risk being entwined in the clutches of Shelob, who lurks within its dank tunnels. It has been known for these bands to be set upon by lesser spiders, and sometimes they manage to fend off and 'control' them for long enough that they can utilise them against their enemies in times of need.

heroUpgrades.name: Animosity
heroUpgrades.flavour: The Orc and Uruk-hai stationed at Cirith Ungol despise one another and will take any chance to prove they are better than the other.

notes.text: The Spider may not be one of the three starting Heroes during Company Creation.
Obviously, this is no mere Spider from Mirkwood but a spawn of something far more sinister. . . .

oath.text: Up in the dark stair, where Orc and Uruk snarl across the same fire, I have the whip and the watch. This rabble will be called {name}, and we will guard the pass or die cursing.

companies.name: Minas Morgul
companies.description:
Once a proud city of Gondor, Minas Morgul has long been under the Dark Lord's control. Now known as the Tower of Sorcery, Minas Morgul is the home of the Nazgûl and their legions of Orcs, spirits and other creatures. The dead city is not a place that any would willingly venture into, except those under the direct influence of the Nazgûl.

As the Dark Lord's search for the Ring of Power continues, the Nazgûl constantly send their own followers to tread the paths of Middle-earth in search of the Ring. Alongside the Orcs that are commonplace within Mordor, the Nazgûl send small numbers of highly skilled Black Númenóreans to take charge of these companies and to make sure the Orcs stay in line.

heroUpgrades.name: Morgul Weaponry
heroUpgrades.flavour: The weapons forged within the citadel of Minas Morgul are infused with malice and dark sorcery, powerful enough to drain the living.

notes.text: Morgul Stalkers & Spectres are On Their Own Path (pg. 33).

oath.text: The Nine rule the Tower of Sorcery, and I serve in the cold green light. Let our name be spoken in whispers, {name}, and let the living tremble as our host marches out of the vale.

effects.text: Morgul Stalkers & Spectres are On Their Own Path (pg. 33).

companies.name: Angmar & Carn Dum
companies.description:
As the power of the Witch-king of Angmar grew, the realm of Arnor began to wain. Its once proud cities fell into ruin and disrepair, a prime target for the forces of Angmar to assail and conquer. Under the Witch-king's command, Orc warbands would attack these fallen cities, delivering them to their dark ruler; for only a few Orcs would be needed to prise these cities from the depleted forces of Arnor.

These warbands were led by the most opportunistic of all the Angmar Orcs, those whose main aim is to plunder, backstab and murder their way to the head of the Witch-king's armies. Yet there were more than mere Orcs in these warbands. Often the relentless cries of the Orcs lured to them the spirits of those long since dead. Now bound to the power of the Witch-king, these spirits would sometimes fight alongside the living – if the Witch-king willed it.

heroUpgrades.name: Show of Strength
heroUpgrades.flavour: Fueled by the dark power of the Witch-king, the hero is a force to be reckoned with when they hit their stride.

notes.text: Spectres and Werewolves are On Their Own Path (pg. 33).

oath.text: The Witch-king has raised the old realm of ice and ruin, and I carry his will into the snow. We who serve the black throne are {name}, and the last kingdoms of the North shall break.

effects.text: Spectres and Werewolves are On Their Own Path (pg. 33).

companies.name: Burning of the Westfold
companies.description:
In the opening act, Isengard turned its eyes to its borders where the Rohirrim called home. Sending the Hill Tribes of Dunland into a frenzy and supplementing them with Uruk and Orc alike, the Westfold never stood a chance.

Now these raiding parties further Saruman's will by taking to the field in further-reaching campaigns all with the same objective in mind: burn them all.

heroUpgrades.name: Pillager
heroUpgrades.flavour: A master of countless raids, this raider knows how best to leverage the desperation their prey feels when the winter's stock is in danger.

notes.text: Feral Uruk-hai and Crebain are On Their Own Path (pg. 33).

oath.text: Fire and axe go before us, and the farms of the Westfold will feed our torches. I drive these raiders onward under the name {name}, and every hall in Rohan shall smell our smoke.

effects.text: Feral Uruk-hai and Crebain are On Their Own Path (pg. 33).

companies.name: Muster of Isengard
companies.description:
As the White Wizard has fallen from grace, Isengard has done much the same. Gone are the trees and the green fields; uprooted, destroyed and replaced by machines and industry. The fires of Isengard never cease, the forges constantly churning out weapons, armour and contraptions of war in order to arm Saruman's fighting Uruk-hai against the races of Men, Elves and Dwarves.

Saruman regularly sends forth companies of Uruk-hai to raid and burn the villages of Men, spreading fear and panic to increase the Wizard's dominance. None felt this more than the land of Rohan, whose settlements and villages were burned to the ground by these bands. The Uruk-hai who lead these warbands are vicious and bloodthirsty warriors, the very best of Saruman's fledgling army, looking to prove themselves worthy to lead the White Wizard's eventual siege upon Helm's Deep.

companies.name: Wolves of Isengard
companies.description:
The wolves of Isengard are the scouts of Saruman's army, used by the Wizard to ambush and harass his enemies. The sound of baying Wargs heralds the imminent arrival of Isengard's wolves, and few who witness their arrival will live to tell the tale. Those who lead the packs are ambitious and cunning Orcs who see their position as an opportunity to carve out a greater standing for themselves, gaining the pick of the plunder and giving their Wargs the freshest of the kills.

These Warg packs also contain Wargs that are yet unridden, either because they are too unruly or have not yet been brought under the heel of the Orcs that ride their trained counterparts. Saruman's Warg Riders will cover much of Middle-earth, always in search of fresh kills and possessions that will aid the White Wizard in his aim to wield The One Ring.

heroUpgrades.name: Savage Charge
heroUpgrades.flavour: The Wolves of Isengard charge with reckless abandon and enough force to send even cavalry sprawling to the ground.

heroUpgrades.name: Feral Charge
heroUpgrades.flavour: Those who are unfortunate to find themselves in front of a Warg's jaws will soon meet a gruesome end.

companies.name: Hill Tribes of Dunland
companies.description:
When Saruman's treachery was finally revealed, he called upon more than just Orcs and Uruk-hai to wage war upon the kingdom of Rohan. The Dunlending people have hated the Rohirrim for centuries, and they required little persuasion to join the White Wizard's cause to see to the destruction of those they have fought to supplant for many years.

Whilst most of the Dunlendings joined Saruman's standing armies, some smaller bands were gathered together and sent out to raid the settlements of Rohan in secret, causing panic before the main armies of Isengard would attack. These bands would often venture into the wider lands of Middle-earth in order to raid and pillage other settlements, gaining wealth and renown amongst their people as they slaughtered those in their path.

heroUpgrades.name: Whipped into a Frenzy
heroUpgrades.flavour: The Hill Tribesmen have been driven into a frenzy by the promise of claiming the lands they believe to be theirs.

oath.text: The Rohirrim took our valleys and stained our fathers' graves, and now a white wizard pays us for our vengeance. Let our hill-fires be named {name}, and let every stolen field be won back in blood.

companies.name: Sharkey's Rogues
companies.description:
Following his army's defeat at Helm's Deep, and his subsequent banishment from Isengard, Saruman secretly made his way west to the Shire, under the guise of an old withered man with the name of Sharkey. Here he set about gathering Ruffians and wild men to him, hatching a scheme to take control over the Shire and the Halflings that lived there as vengeance for the defeat that the Travellers had brought upon him.

After plotting and buying his way into control over the Shire, Sharkey assumed full command under the name of 'The Chief' and sent bands of his Ruffians across the Shire and surrounding lands to spread his will. Some of these groups of Ruffians and wild men would often venture a bit further than instructed to bully local villages, especially if there was some extra money to be had.

companies.name: Moria
companies.description:
Since the coming of the Balrog and the rout of the Dwarves, Moria's halls have resounded to the clamour of a different kind. Sonorous drum beats and the gleeful cackle of Goblin-kin echo where once hammer fell and harps were played. Unlike the realms of Man and Orc, Moria is a domain constantly driven by internal strife, as the fractious Goblins who dwell there jostle for power and wealth with one another, and battles are fought between rival factions for control of a particular hall or possession of some tarnished treasure or another.

In the deeps of Moria, gaining power is no easy thing, and holding onto it is even harder – any Goblin with aspirations to rule will fight to rally followers to their cause, while the many self-styled Goblin kings will unleash their warbands to forage for supplies and treasure (with which they can lure in more Goblins to their cause). This chaotic situation inevitably means there is no shortage of Goblins patrolling not only the mines of Moria, but for leagues around in every direction, fighting against Men, Elves and Dwarves, but also each other in their self-defeating quest for supremacy.

heroUpgrades.flavour: Those few individuals spiteful enough to rise through the ranks are willing to do whatever is necessary to secure victory, even at the cost of their own forces.

companies.description:
Since the fall of Greenwood the Great into the darkness now known as Mirkwood, the power of the Necromancer has turned the fauna ever deeper toward his will. Spiders, Wargs, and orcish kind gather to lay siege to the Elven kingdoms that make up the Northern realms.

From the depths of the Misty Mountains, goblins pour forth with powerful sorcery. Orcs from Mordor, splintering off from the war effort or sent purposefully, unite with the goblins and beasts to form companies in this additional warfront.

heroUpgrades.name: Cover of Darkness
heroUpgrades.flavour: Using a powerful sorcery known to the Dark Lord himself, cloud coverage blots out the sunlight.

companies.name: Harad
companies.description:
In the vast desert wastes of Harad, large kingdoms and realms are a rare thing to find. Most Haradrim live in small tribes, each with its own hierarchy, which lies under the influence of greater warlords. The chieftains of these tribes possess a ruthless streak, a necessity in Harad for those who wish to keep their power and not meet an untimely death.

Haradrim who live in these tribes will form raiding parties, bands of cruel Men that ride out to pillage and raid the outposts and southernmost settlements of Gondor and her Fiefdoms. These raids are often quick and bloody, with many good Men being felled by the Haradrim's black-fletched arrows. Although these acts of war are born out of need to gather provisions to survive, it has since become ingrained into Haradrim culture, with raiding parties constantly heading out as much for enjoyment than anything else.

heroUpgrades.flavour: The hero has mastered the study of the vile toxins of the Haradrim, and coats the blades of their weapons in the most potent of these.

companies.name: City of Umbar
companies.description:
Umbar is a ruthless city where treachery and corruption run rife within its shadowed streets. None that reside there better represent this than the Corsairs who man Umbar's fleets. The captains of these ships are tyrannical and greedy Men, who will sail the coasts of Gondor and even further with the intent of pillaging the settlements upon the shores.

The crew under these captains' command will often share their lust for plunder, and need little convincing to set off upon the black-sailed ships in search of new settlements to raze to the ground. Once this band of malicious Men has raided a town, stealing whatever they can lay their hands on, they will splinter into smaller bands, each eager to unleash their own devious brand of destruction and murder upon the villages along the coast. The more fear these bands of Evil Men can instill in their enemies, the higher they will rise up the treacherous ranks of the Corsair fleets.

companies.name: Easterlings
companies.description:
It is said of the Easterlings that there is no Mannish culture in Middle-earth so devoted to warfare, with every Easterling, male and female, learning to fight with spear and sword from their youth. Those who take their devotion to martial matters further will supplicate themselves at one of the many warrior shrines across the land, learning the art of bladecraft under the brutal tutelage of the Dragon Knights, in the hope of one day being raised to become one of their chosen 'Black Dragons'. To this end, aspirants will venture forth from their warrior shrine to test themselves, either against other shrines or, preferably, against the dwellers of other lands.

A warband that succeeds in this task does not become rich in the conventional sense, for wealth is of no consequence to those who walk the blade-path. Indeed, any treasures plucked from the fallen are offered to their shrine as proof of their feats in battle. Victories inevitably draw more like-minded soldiers to their ranks, and while many warbands dwindle through defeat, the greatest will return back to their shrine triumphant, faces scarred from battle and their packs bulging with trophies taken from the vanquished.

companies.name: Grand Army of the South
companies.description:
The people of Khand have long been allied with the Dark Lord of Mordor, their 'friendship' with the dark tower having proven extremely profitable over the many years. The Khandish warriors are mercenaries at heart, happy to fight for whomever will pay them the most. Far to the south of Gondor, even further than the Haradrim, dwell the Mahûd, a vicious warrior race. There are few who can survive in the harsh desert environment that the Mahûd have adapted to, and those unaccustomed to the scorching heat and arid terrain will succumb to thirst and exhaustion should they remain there for too long.

The Dark Lord's call has summoned all manner of creatures to his banner, including these Men of self-interest looking for extra coin in exchange for their club or axe. While never neighbors before, they now frequently share camp during the War of the Ring.

companies.name: Dol Guldur
companies.description:
Within the southern reaches of the Greenwood, the old fortress of Dol Guldur was long thought to have been abandoned many years ago. As the years of the Third Age rolled on, a darkness fell upon its ruined walls. It was believed that a sorcerer now dwelt within its crumbling foundations, and that Evil emanated from it. In time, the woodsmen would no longer call the forest Greenwood. It would become known by a new name – Mirkwood.

The truth was far worse than even the woodsmen could have imagined, for it was no mere sorcerer who dwelt within Dol Guldur, but the Dark Lord himself. Sauron had drawn all manner of Orcs and Wargs to his power, including the forces of Azog the Defiler. The Pale Orc still thirsted for the blood of Thorin Oakenshield, and news of the company's travels had reached the Orc's ears. With this new knowledge, Azog would send out warbands of Orcs and Wargs in search of the Dwarven travellers, their sole purpose to obtain the head of Thorin Oakenshield.

companies.name: Goblin-Town
companies.description:
Whilst the Goblin-infested realm of Moria is splintered into countless factions all vying for their place at the top, the neighbouring realm of Goblin-town suffers no such problems. For atop the throne of this blighted kingdom sits the bloated Goblin King, a vile and ruthless leader who towers over his Goblin subjects.

The Goblins under their king's rule are constantly sent out on hunting parties to cause destruction in the Goblin King's name, or to quell those that would plot to overthrow their blubbery overlord. Yet in more recent years, news of the price put upon the head of Thorin Oakenshield has seen these hunting parties put to a different use; hunting down the would-be Dwarf king and bringing him to his knees before The Goblin King.

At the northernmost peaks of The Misty Mountains lies the fortress of Gundabad, the gateway to the fell kingdom of Angmar. Within its walls are harboured hosts of Gundabad Orcs, monsters and other vicious creatures, bred specifically for the purpose of waging war upon the enemies of the Dark Lord.

Under the orders of Bolg, the Castellan of Mount Gundabad, small bands of Orcs and other foul creatures ventured forth from the fortress' bowels in order to wreak havoc and destruction upon Middle-earth. These bands attacked outposts, raided settlements and engaged travelling warbands in brutal melee, all in the name of the Dark Lord.

items.name: Aura of Command
items.definition: This Magical Power targets the caster. Whilst this power is in effect, the caster and all friendly models within 6" automatically pass all Courage tests they are required to make.

items.name: Aura of Dismay
items.definition: This Magical Power targets the caster. Enemy models within 6" of the caster suffer a -1 penalty to any Courage Tests they are required to take.

items.name: Banishment

items.name: Black Dart

items.name: Bladewrath
items.definition: This Magical Power targets one friendly model within range. In the ensuing Fight phase, all Strikes made by the target model are resolved at Strength 6, regardless of any other modifiers.

items.name: Blessing of the Valar
items.definition: This Magical Power targets one friendly model within range. The target immediately regains 1 Fate point spent earlier in the battle.

items.name: Blinding Light
items.definition: This Magical Power targets the caster. Whilst the power is in effect, the area within 6" of the caster is always considered to be daylight (perfect if you are playing a battle at night). Additionally, whilst this power is in effect, enemy models that make a Shooting Attack that targets a model within 6" of the caster will only hit on a To Hit Roll of a 6. Models cannot benefit from this Magical Power if there is a piece of impassable terrain, such as a wall or building, directly between all parts of the model and the source of the light.

items.name: Call Winds
items.definition: This Magical Power targets one enemy model within range. The target is immediately blown D3 + 3" directly away from the caster in a straight line. If the model comes into contact with another model or piece of terrain, then it immediately stop. After it has been blown back, the target is knocked Prone. If the target was Engaged in Combat, the effect is the same and they can be blown out of Combat.

items.name: Chill Soul
items.definition: This Magical Power targets one enemy model in range. The target model immediately suffers 1 Wound. If this Magical Power targets a Cavalry model, the caster must choose whether the rider or the mount is the target.

items.name: Collapse Rocks
items.definition: This Magical Power targets one enemy model in range that is within a ruin, stone or brick building, cave, rock pile or some other piece of terrain where the caster could crack rocks either underfoot or overhead. The target suffers one Strength 7 hit and is knocked Prone. If the target was a Cavalry model, they will automatically count as suffering the Knocked Flying result on the Thrown Rider Chart.

items.name: Compel
items.definition: This Magical Power targets one enemy model in range. The caster may Move the target up to half its maximum Move Value, even if the target has already Moved this turn. They cannot Move the target out of Combat, make them take a Jump, Climb, Leap or Swim Test, lie them down or make them dismount. They can, however, make them Move into Difficult Terrain or Charge an enemy model (if able), in which case no Courage Test would be required to Charge an enemy with the Terror special rule. They can make the target drop an Object they are carrying as part of a Scenario (but not Wargear) or put on the One Ring if they carry it. Once the target has been Moved, it cannot Move any further that turn for any reason but may otherwise act normally. If the model affected by this Magical Power would normally have to Charge as part of their Move, they are not forced to when under the influence of this Magical Power.

items.name: Curse
items.definition: This Magical Power targets one enemy model in range. The target immediately loses 1 Fate point. If this Magical Power targets a Cavalry model, the caster must choose whether the rider or the mount is the target.

items.name: Drain Courage
