This Magical Power targets one enemy model in range. The target immediately becomes paralysed. A Paralysed model immediately becomes Prone and may do nothing until it recovers. This includes Activating, making Shooting Attacks, declaring Heroic Actions or using Active abilities. If a Paralysed model is Engaged in Combat, it may contribute no dice to the Duel Roll, and does not provide its Fight Value - it may also not make Strikes or stand up if its side wins. If a Paralysed model is the only model from its side involved in a Combat, then it automatically loses the Duel Roll - no dice are rolled.
                
                At the end of the End Phase of each turn, a Paralysed model may roll a D6. On a 6, the model immediately recovers (they may use Might to improve this roll). Additionally, after making this roll, any friendly model in base contact with a Paralysed model may roll a D6 one at a time. If any model rolls a 6, the Paralysed model immediately recovers (a Hero model may use their own Might to improve this roll.)
                
                If a Paralysed model is in a water feature at the end of the Move Phase, then it must take a Swim Test to see if it sinks.

items.name: Protection of the Valar
items.definition: This Magical Power targets one friendly model within range. The target cannot be chosen as the target of an enemy Magical Power or enemy special rule that specifically targets a model. Additionally, enemy models that target the protected model with a Shooting attack will suffer a -1 penalty to the to hit Roll.

items.name: Renew
items.definition: This Magical Power targets one friendly model in range. The target immediately regains 1 Wound lost earlier in the battle.If this Magical Power targets a Cavalry model, the caster must choose whether the rider or the mount is the target.

items.name: Sorcerous Blast
items.definition:
This Magical Power targets one enemy model within range. The target immediately suffers one Strength 5 hit. If they survive, the target is immediately knocked Prone. If the target was a Cavalry model, they will automatically count as suffering the Knocked Flying result on the Thrown Rider Chart.
                
                If the target was Engaged in Combat, then any other model that is also engaged in the same Combat will also be knocked prone if it has a Strength of 5 or lower - make sure to Pair Off Combats before working out which models are knocked prone in this manner.

items.name: Strengthen Will
items.definition: This Magical Power targets one friendly model within range.The target immediately regains a single Will Point spent earlier in the battle. If this Magical Power targets a Cavalry model, the caster must choose whether the rider or the mount is the target.

items.name: Terrifying Aura
items.definition: This Magical Power targets the caster themselves. Whilst this Magical Power is in effect, the caster has the Terror special rule.

items.name: Transfix
items.definition: This Magical Power targets one enemy model in range. Until the End Phase of the turn, the target cannot Activate, declare Heroic Actions, use Active Abilities, or make Shooting Attacks. If the target wins a Duel Roll, they may not make Strikes. if the target has a piece of wargear that has an Active ability, they stilll have that piece of wargear but cannot use the ability tied to it.

items.name: Tremor
items.definition:
Draw an imaginary line that extends D3+3" directly away from the caster in a direction chosen by the caster. This Magical Power targets every model (friend of foe) that lies under the line. Each target immediately suffers one Strength 4 hit and is knocked Prone; if the target was a Cavalry model, they will automatically count as suffering the Knocked Flying result on the Thrown Rider Chart. If a target is Engaged in Combat, then all other models in the same Combat are also considered to be a target - make sure to Pair Off Combats before working out which models are a target.
                
                Models with the Fly special rule can never be a target of this Magical Power under any circumstances.

items.name: Wither
items.definition: This Magical Power targets one enemy model in range. The target immediately reduces their Strength value by 1 for the remainder of the game. A model can be affected by this Magical Power multiple times over the course of the battle, reducing its Strength value each time. Should a model ever have its Strength reduced to 0, they are immediately slain and removed as a casualty. If this Magical Power targets a Cavalry model, the caster must choose whether the rider or the Mount is the target.

items.name: Wrath of Bruinen
items.definition: This Magical Power targets all enemy models within range, even if they are not in Line of Sight of the caster. All target models immediately suffer one Strength 2 hit and are knocked Prone. Cavalry models are automatically treated as suffering a Knocked Flying result on the Thrown Rider Chart. If a target is within a water feature, they will suffer one Strength 8 hit instead of one Strength 2 hit.

items.name: Writhing Vines
items.definition: This Magical Power targets the caster. Place a 25mm Vine Marker wholly within 3" of the caster. Enemy models treat the area within 3" of the Vine Marker as Difficult Terrain. Remove the Vine Marker during the End Phase.

items.name: Your Staff is Broken
items.definition: This Magical Power targets one enemy model that has a Staff of Power within range. The target's Staff of Power is immediately destroyed - remove it from their wargear.

wargear.text: The most common types of wargear available to models in a Battle Company. Each entry has an Influence cost and a rating (warrior / hero). If the Hero's faction uses a lower/higher point value for a Warrior, use that for the first (warrior) value instead. Elven-made weaponry uses the generic equivalent values but is restricted to Elf models unless otherwise noted. Companies may list additional wargear on their page.

armourUpgrade.text: Upgrade Armour by one stage. Each upgrade costs 1 Influence and adds (1 / 5) rating.

restrictions: Warrior models follow their usual Options rules and may only purchase items that fit that list. A Warrior may drop Wargear provided it keeps a legal Option, or buys a new legal Option.

Hero models are not bound to Warrior Options. They can purchase any wargear available to any member of their Battle Company, including those that could be promoted or join as Reinforcements; but not those that joined by other means. Some options are explicitly unique to certain profiles and are not in this table. A piece of wargear gained through other means does not let Heroes buy the same type.
Heroes need to take note of the rules for Shields being cumbersome (MESBG rules manual, p. 110).
wargear.beasts: Models with the Beast keyword may not take additional wargear other than upgrading their Armour and may only carry Equipment that exclusively gives a Special Rule (e.g. Trophy Pelt).

equipment.text: Equipment is not as restricted as wargear as to who can take it, but some pieces can only be purchased by certain companies, only by Heroes, or only by Good or Evil models. The number in brackets is the rating the item adds (warrior / hero, like the Armoury). A model may only carry one Large and one Small piece of Equipment. Equipment is lost if its owner is slain.

items.name: Backpack
items.definition: A model with a Backpack may carry an additional three Small pieces of Equipment within it (for a maximum of four).

items.name: Badge of Courage
items.definition: A model with a Badge of Courage gains the Fearless special rule.

items.name: Barding
items.definition: The rider gains the Expert Rider & Horselord special rules.

items.name: Climbing ropes
items.definition: A model with Climbing Ropes will add +1 to any Climb tests they make. Additionally, after the model makes a Climb test they may choose to leave their rope behind. If they do so they cannot use it for the rest of the game, mark the location with a marker, counter or token. Any friendly model that makes a Climb test from the same point also gains a bonus of +1 to the result. At the end of the game, the model is assumed to retrieve the rope.

items.name: Company Drum
items.definition: This is a War Drum that grants the bearer the Command Support keyword.

items.name: Company Horn
items.definition: This is a War Horn that grants the bearer the Command Support keyword.

items.name: Company Standard
items.definition: This is a Pennant that grants the bearer the Command Support keyword. Friendly models within 3" of this model may re-roll any rolls of a 1 when making a Duel Roll.

items.name: Company Instrument
items.definition: This is an Instrument that grants the bearer the Command Support keyword. Friendly models within 3" of this model that suffer a wound may roll a d6. On a natural 6, they ignore the wound.

items.name: Concealing Cloak
items.definition: A model wearing a Concealing Cloak has the Stalk Unseen special rule.

items.name: Dwarven Brew
items.definition: A model may elect to use their Dwarven Brew at the start of any game, if they do so, every model within the model's Battle Company adds +1 to their Courage value for the remainder of the game. Once used, take an Intelligence Test. On an unsuccessful roll, the keg has run dry; remove it from the Hero model's Equipment.

items.name: Envenom Weapon (X)
items.definition: When a model purchases Envenom Weapon, they must decide which weapon on their profile they will grant the Poisoned Attacks special rule.

items.name: Healing Herbs
items.definition: A Hero may elect to use their Healing Herbs at the end of any game they participated in that they were not removed as a casualty (ignoring Fleeing the Battlefield). If they do this, remove the Healing Herbs from their Equipment. All members of the Battle Company may add +1 to any Injury rolls that they must make at the end of the game. This is not cumulative.

items.name: Lucky Talisman
items.definition: A Hero with a Lucky Talisman may re-roll any failed Fate rolls.

items.name: Map
items.definition: After both Battle Companies have deployed, before the first Priority is rolled, a Battle Company with a Map may redeploy D6 models using the normal rules. If both players have a Map, the player with Priority redeploys their models first. In scenarios where you roll for when or where models arrive or deploy, you may modify the roll for this model by +1 or -1. In scenarios where the bearer would be grouped with other models for these rolls, then they may confer this bonus to the whole group.

items.name: Mountain Boots
items.definition: A model wearing Mountain Boots has the Mountain Dweller special rule.

items.name: Ring of Warding
items.definition: A model with a Ring of Warding gains the Resistant to Magic special rule.

items.name: Scroll of Courage
items.definition: At the start of any game, the Hero may read the Scroll of Courage. If they do, all friendly models add +1 to their Courage value for the remainder of the game. Once read, take an Intelligence Test. On an unsuccessful roll, the scroll is caught by a strong breeze and floats off into the air; remove it from the Hero model's Equipment.

items.name: Scroll of Hidden Paths
items.definition: At the start of any game, before forces are deployed, the Hero may read the Scroll of Hidden Paths. If they do, you may keep D3 Warrior models off the board when deploying your forces. These models will arrive from any board edge of your choosing at the end of your company's second Move phase via the rules for Reinforcements. Once read, take an Intelligence Test. On an unsuccessful roll, the scroll is caught by a strong breeze and floats off into the air; remove it from the Hero model's Equipment.

items.name: Seeing Stone
items.definition: Once per game, during the Priority Phase but before the roll for Priority, the bearer can use the Palantir to automatically win the roll to choose who has Priority for that turn. If both sides have a special rule allowing them to do this and both wish to use it in the same turn, players roll off as normal and both special rules count as being used.

items.name: Small Shield
items.definition: This is a Light Shield that gives the bearer +1 to their Defence Characteristic against Strikes. This may not be carried in conjunction with another kind of Shield.

items.name: Torching Brand
items.definition: A model with a Torch gains the following benefits: They illuminate the area within 6" of them; models within this area can be seen as if it were daylight. They gain the Terror (Beast) and Terror (Cavalry) special rules. They gain Dominant (2).

items.name: Traps & Snares
items.definition: A model with Traps & Snares gains the Master of Traps special rule (page 19 of the Armies of Middle-Earth manual)

items.name: Trophy Pelt
items.definition: A model with a Trophy Pelt gains the Terror special rule.

items.name: Wondrous Cram
items.definition: A model that has purchased Wondrous Cram may elect to use it at the end of any game they participated in that they were removed as a casualty (ignoring Fleeing the Battlefield). If they do this, remove the Wondrous Cram from their Equipment; additionally, do not roll on the Injury chart for them, instead they will automatically count as having rolled the Full Recovery result.

items.name: Woodland Belt
items.definition: A model wearing the Woodland Belt has the Woodland Creature special rule.

creatures.text: A purchased Creature must be attached to the Leader or one of the Sergeants - it does not take a space on the roster. Each Hero may only ever have a single Creature (max. 3 in the company). Creatures are On Their Own Path and do not roll on any Injury chart if slain; a Creature is only Dead if the Hero it is attached to would be. Creatures are never considered to be unarmed.

wanderers.text: A Battle Company may only ever have one Wanderer at a time. Wanderers cannot buy additional wargear or Equipment. They are Heroes in all ways with these exceptions: they cannot gain Experience Points or receive Advancements; they do not provide a Stand Fast!; they may not affect members of the Battle Company with their Heroic Actions (e.g. calling "With Me!").

keywords.name: Spy
keywords.definition: At the beginning of the game, after both sides have deployed, this Hero may choose one enemy Hero in your opponent's Company. Whilst this Hero is within 12" of, and has Line of Sight to, the chosen Hero, whenever the chosen Hero declares a Heroic Action they must roll a D6. On a 1-2, the Heroic Action is immediately cancelled and the Might Point is not spent. The chosen Hero may not then attempt to declare the same Heroic Action again that turn.

keywords.name: Gatekeeper
keywords.definition: At the end of the Priority Phase, this Hero may spend a Will Point to use this special rule. If they do, this Hero may select a single enemy Infantry model within 6" and Line of Sight and roll a D6. On a 3+, the chosen model may not Move during their Activation, but may otherwise act normally. Monster models are unaffected by this special rule.

keywords.name: Heroic Move Mastery
keywords.definition: If during the Declare Heroic Actions step of a Move Phase or Fight Phase, both sides have declared a Heroic Move or a Heroic Combat and a roll-off is required to see which side's Heroic Move happens first, friendly Heroes within 6" of this Hero will gain a bonus to that roll. If they would normally win the roll-off on a 4+, they will instead win it on a 3+. If they would normally win the roll-off on a 1, 2, or 3, they will instead win the roll-off on a 1, 2, 3, or 4.

keywords.name: Longbeard
keywords.definition: During the Priority Phase, after the roll for Priority has taken place, this Hero can spend a Will Point to allow their controlling player to re-roll their roll for Priority.

keywords.name: Reading the Portents
keywords.definition: During the Fight Phase, this Hero can spend a Will Point to allow a friendly model within 6" to re-roll a single die during their Duel Roll. This Hero can use this special rule multiple times during the same Fight Phase, so long as they have Will Points remaining.

keywords.name: Big Game Hunter
keywords.definition: If this Hero successfully Wound an enemy Monster model with a shooting attack (a Wound is caused and is not prevented), it will deal D3 Wounds rather than 1.

keywords.name: Knife Mastery
keywords.definition: Friendly Battle Company models with any bow or crossbow within 3" and Line of Sight of this Hero may reroll To Wound Rolls of a natural 1 when making Strikes. Additionally, friendly Battle Company models with any bow or crossbow within 3" and Line of Sight of this Hero may use the Shielding rule even if they do not possess any kind of shield.

keywords.name: Heroic Shoot Mastery
keywords.definition: When benefiting from a Heroic Shoot called by this Hero, friendly models may reroll failed To Wound Rolls when making shooting attacks.

keywords.name: Swift Shot
keywords.definition: This Hero never suffers the -1 penalty To Hit for Moving and Shooting. May fire a Crossbow after moving up to half of their Movement value, but with a -1 penalty.

keywords.name: Rapid Fire
keywords.definition: If this Hero hits a target with its ranged weapon in the Shoot Phase, it may make another shooting attack with its weapon that targets a model within 3" of the initial target - it may even be the same target. If that second shot also hits, then this model may Shoot again as described above. This model can make a maximum of three shots per turn as a result of this special rule.

keywords.name: A Good Sort
keywords.definition: Whilst within 3" of another friendly Hero, this Hero increases their Attacks by 1 and may re-roll any rolls of a 1 in this Hero's Duel rolls.

keywords.name: Relentless Commander
keywords.definition: Whilst this Hero is alive and on the battlefield, if you win the roll to choose who has Priority, and choose to give Priority to your opponent, then until the end of the turn friendly Battle Company models within 6" of this Hero may reroll To Wound Rolls of a natural 1 when making Strikes.

keywords.name: Heroic Combat Mastery
keywords.definition: The Hero may call Heroic Combat without expending a point of Might if they slayed an enemy model they were Engaged in Combat with in the previous turn.

keywords.name: Fearsome Charge
keywords.definition: If this Hero Charges into Combat, then until the end of the turn they count as having the Terror special rule.

keywords.name: Reckless Charge
keywords.definition: If this Hero Charges into Combat, then must reroll failed To Wound rolls when making Strikes.

keywords.name: Pinpoint Shot
keywords.definition: Instead of shooting normally in the Shoot Phase, this Hero may make a single shooting attack against an enemy model Engaged in Combat with a friendly model (including himself). If they do, then if the To Hit Roll is successful, this Hero doesn't need to make any In The Way Rolls – the shot will automatically hit its target.

keywords.name: "Hold positions, loose the arrows!"
keywords.definition: Whilst within 3" of this Hero, friendly models may re-roll failed To Hit Rolls when making a shooting attack, providing they didn't Move in the preceding Move Phase.

keywords.name: Heroic Accuracy Mastery
keywords.definition: Friendly models benefiting from this Hero's Heroic Accuracy pass in-the-way checks on a 2+ rather than 4+.

keywords.name: Volley Fire
keywords.definition: This Hero increases the range of their shooting attacks by 6", provided they have not moved that turn. This special rule does not apply to throwing weapons.

keywords.name: Lethal Aim
keywords.definition: Each turn during the Shoot Phase, this Hero gains a free Might Point that can only be spent during a shooting attack on either a To Hit Roll, a To Wound Roll, or an In The Way Test. If this free Might Point is not spent by the end of the turn, it is lost.

keywords.name: Usurper of Kings
keywords.definition: If this Hero is Engaged in Combat with an enemy Hero, this Hero may re-roll a single D6 during the Duel Roll. Additionally, this Hero must reroll To Wound Rolls of a natural 1 when making Strikes against an enemy Hero.

keywords.name: Claim the Throne
keywords.definition: If the enemy Leader is removed as a casualty whilst within 6" of this Hero, then for the duration of the battle friendly Battle Company models treat this Hero as a banner with a range of 6".

keywords.name: Heroic Challenge Mastery
keywords.definition: The number of bonus Attacks granted by the Heroic Challenge is increased to +2 for this Hero, rather than the normal +1.

keywords.name: General Hunter
keywords.definition: If this model slays the enemy General in a Combat, they immediately regain a single point of Might spent earlier in the battle.

keywords.name: Cunning Fighter
keywords.definition: If this Hero wins a Duel Roll, and there are no other allies involved in the Combat (including Supporting models) then this Hero can choose a single enemy model on a 25mm base that he was Engaged in Combat with and roll a D6. On a 4+, the chosen model is knocked Prone before Strikes are made.

keywords.name: Deceptive Caster
keywords.definition: At the beginning of the game, after both sides have deployed, this Hero may choose a single enemy Hero. The chosen Hero suffers a -1 penalty to any Resist Tests they take when targeted by a Magical Power Cast by this Hero; except any natural 6.

keywords.name: Heroic Channeling Mastery
keywords.definition: When the Hero casts a Heroic Channeled spell that targets a single model, they may target one additional model.

keywords.name: Sorcerous Adept
keywords.definition: Each time this Hero rolls one or more natural 6s when making a Casting Test, they will regain a single Will Point after resolving the effects of the Magical Power.

keywords.name: Master of Magic
keywords.definition: This Hero may still be Activated whilst Engaged in Combat in order to attempt to Cast Magical Powers whilst Engaged in Combat, with the exception of the following Magical Powers: Nature's Wrath, Sorcerous Blast, Call Winds, and Tremor.

keywords.name: Swift Parry
keywords.definition: This Hero may force one enemy model involved in the same Combat as them to re-roll a single D6 for their Duel Roll. This must be done before all other re-rolls, and before any Might Points are spent.

keywords.name: Marshal
keywords.definition: This Hero and friendly Battle Company Warriors that can draw Line of Sight to this Hero may re-roll any failed Intelligence Tests and gain the Shieldwall special rule.

keywords.name: Heroic Defence Mastery
keywords.definition: The Hero may call Heroic Defence without expending Might if they are outnumbered in Combat.

keywords.name: Defender of the City
keywords.definition: This Hero may use the Shielding special rule even if they are not armed with a shield. If this Hero elects to shield, and wins the ensuing Combat, they may make a single Strike against one enemy model that was involved in the Combat.

keywords.name: The King's Protector
keywords.definition: At the start of the game, choose one friendly Battle Company Hero. If the target Hero is Engaged in Combat and within 6" of this Hero, this Hero may declare a Heroic Combat for free. If the Heroic Combat is successful then this Hero must use the following Move to join the target Hero's combat. If this is not possible, then this Hero must Move as close as possible to the target Hero.

keywords.name: Experienced Tracker
keywords.definition: At the start of each game, you may choose either Woodland Creature or Mountain Dwellers. Friendly Battle Company models gain the chosen special rule for the duration of the game.

keywords.name: Heroic March Mastery
keywords.definition: Models are not required to stay within the 'At the Double' range of this Hero in a turn in which this Hero declares a Heroic March.

keywords.name: Chief Advisor
keywords.definition: Whenever a friendly Battle Company Hero model within 6" spends a Might Point, they may roll a D6. On a natural 6, the Might Point is free and is not spent.

keywords.name: Rallying Cry
keywords.definition: Friendly Battle Company Infantry models can still charge after participating in a Heroic March called by this Hero.

keywords.name: Furious Tirade
keywords.definition: Enemy Warrior models cannot benefit from a Hero model's Stand Fast whilst within 6" of this Hero.

keywords.name: Commanding Bellow
keywords.definition: Friendly Battle Company models treat this Hero as a banner with a range of 3".

keywords.name: Heroic Resolve Mastery
keywords.definition: The Hero may call Heroic Resolve without expending Might if their force is Broken.

keywords.name: Voice of Command
keywords.definition: The range of this Hero's Stand Fast is 12" rather than 6". Additionally, friendly Hero models can benefit from this Hero's Stand Fast.

keywords.name: Burly
keywords.definition: A model with this special rule does not suffer the -1 penalty to the Duel Roll for using a two-handed weapon. Additionally, a model with this special rule can still Move its full Move Value whilst carrying a Heavy Object.

keywords.name: To Arms!
keywords.definition: Once per game, at the start of his Activation, this Hero can declare they are using this special rule. If they do, then until the end of the turn all friendly models within 3" of this Hero increase their Strength by 1.

keywords.name: Heroic Strength Mastery
keywords.definition: When this Hero declares a Heroic Strength, they may choose to make a single Strike against every enemy involved in the combat, including supporting models, instead of making Strikes as normal.

keywords.name: Oblivious to Pain
keywords.definition: Whenever this Hero suffers a Wound, roll a D6. On the roll of natural 6, the Wound is ignored.

keywords.name: Fury of the Bear
keywords.definition: If this Hero is involved in a Combat and kills every model he was Engaged in Combat with, then in the following turn he may declare a Heroic Move for free and must Charge if able.

keywords.name: Grim Blade
keywords.definition: This Hero will always win the roll-off during a Drawn Combat. If both sides have a Hero with this special rule, neither side will benefit from this special rule.

keywords.name: For Glory
keywords.definition: Once per game, at the start of any Fight Phase, this Hero can use this special rule so long as they are alive and on the battlefield. If they do, then friendly Battle Company models within 6" of this Hero gain a bonus of +1 Fight Value and may reroll To Wound Rolls of a natural 1 when making Strikes until the end of the turn.

keywords.name: Heroic Strike Mastery
keywords.definition: When calling a Heroic Strike the Hero adds +3 to their Fight Value rather than rolling a D3.

keywords.name: Master Duelist
keywords.definition: At the start of a Combat involving this Hero, before any Heroic Strikes are resolved, this Hero may increase their Fight Value to match that of a single enemy model they are Engaged in Combat with.

keywords.name: Warrior of Renown
keywords.definition: Enemy models Engaged in Combat with this Hero cannot declare a Heroic Strike.

keywords.name: The Charge of Gondor
keywords.definition: This Hero gains a bonus of +1 to their Fight Value in a Combat in which they have charged.

keywords.name: Remember Today
keywords.definition: This Hero may use the Might, Will, and Fate points of another friendly Hero within 3".

keywords.name: Lord of Dol Amroth
keywords.definition: Other friendly Dol Amroth models treat this Hero as a banner with a range of 6".

keywords.name: Lord of Lossarnach
keywords.definition: Other friendly Lossarnach models within 3" of this Hero may re-roll To Wound Rolls of a natural 1 when making Strikes.

keywords.name: Chief of Lamedon
keywords.definition: Other friendly Lamedon models within 3" of this Hero automatically pass any Courage Tests they are required to take.

keywords.name: Lord of the Vale
keywords.definition: Other friendly models within 3" of this Hero may re-roll To Hit Rolls of a 1 when making a shooting attack in the Shoot Phase, provided they did not Move in the preceding Move Phase.

keywords.name: Defiance
keywords.definition: This Hero cannot have their Courage value reduced by enemy special rules or Magical Powers.

keywords.name: Foresight of the Seer
keywords.definition: Whenever this Hero suffers a Wound, roll a D6. On the roll of a natural 6, the Wound is ignored. If this Hero would later gain a special rule with the same effect (e.g. Oblivious to Pain) then treat that special rule as improving Foresight of the Seer to a natural 5+.

keywords.name: There Were Some Who Resisted
keywords.definition: The Hero may re-roll any dice that roll a 1 when making Courage Tests. Númenór Stands Alone! If you wish to represent Númenór by themselves, simply ignore any reference to Rivendell Warriors and use the Custom Selection Optional Rule to take exclusively Warriors of Númenór.

keywords.name: Back on your Horses!
keywords.definition: If the Hero started the scenario as a Cavalry model they may benefit from the following rule: At the end of this Hero's move, if they are in base contact with a friendly Cavalry Warrior model who is not Engaged in Combat, then the Warrior may give the Hero their horse. Replace the Warrior model with a suitable dismount, and replace the Hero with their original mounted version. The Warrior will be placed in the same place the Hero was, and vice versa. The Hero will only count as riding a standard horse after using this rule.

keywords.name: One Final Blow
keywords.definition: If this Hero is slain, they may immediately make one Strike on each enemy model that was Engaged with them using their base Strength.

keywords.name: Know All Paths
keywords.definition: This Hero and their Mount, if applicable, gain the Woodland Creature special rule.

keywords.name: Lordly Quality
keywords.definition: Friendly models that share the same faction keyword treat this Hero as a banner.

keywords.name: Defender
keywords.definition: At the beginning of the Fight Phase, at the start of the Declare Heroic Actions step, if a friendly Hero with the opposite species keyword (Man/Dwarf) would be considered Trapped and is in a different Combat than this Hero, then this Hero may declare a Heroic Combat for free. If this Heroic Combat is successful, then this Hero must use the following Move to join the other's Combat. If not possible, then this Hero must Move as close as possible to each other.

keywords.name: Blessing of the Golden Wood
keywords.definition: The Hero may re-roll any failed Fate rolls.

keywords.name: Veteran of the Old Wars
keywords.definition: This Hero gains the Terror special rule.

keywords.name: Bladelord
keywords.definition: If they are Outnumbered in a Combat, this Hero may reroll To Wound Rolls of a natural 1 when making Strikes. If they have the Infantry keyword and are Outnumbered in a Combat, this Hero may instead re-roll all failed To Wound Rolls when making Strikes.

keywords.name: The Stubbornness of Dwarves
keywords.definition: During a Duel roll, before any rerolls are used, if the opposing player rolled more dice in the combat then the Hero may reroll a single d6 as part of the Duel roll.

keywords.name: Stubborn Brilliance!
keywords.definition: The Hero gains the Master of Battle (5+) special rule.

keywords.name: Moneybags
keywords.definition: At the start of the Fight phase, before any Heroic Actions are declared, the Hero can spend a Will Point to use this special rule. If he does, then any friendly Lake-town models within 6" of this Hero gains a bonus of +1 to their Fight Value and treats this Hero as a banner until the end of the turn.

keywords.name: You Have My Sword
keywords.definition: During the Declare Heroic Actions step of the Fight Phase, if a friendly Hobbit is Engaged in Combat and is within 6" of this Hero, this Hero may declare a free Heroic Combat. If this Heroic Combat is successful, then this Hero must use the following Move to join the Hobbit's Combat. If this is not possible, then this Hero must Move as close as possible to the Hobbit. This Hero cannot use this special rule if they are engaged in the same Combat as the Hobbit in question.

keywords.name: I Have My Own Sword, Thank You Very Much
keywords.definition: This model may re-roll any failed To Wound rolls when making Strikes.

keywords.name: Of a Party Sort
keywords.definition: The Hero will pass a Fate Roll on a 3+ rather than a 4+. Additionally, the Hero may re-roll failed Fate Rolls.

keywords.name: Throwing Stones
keywords.definition: Instead of using the Throw Stones special rule as normal, the Hero may use stones in the same way as a Throwing Weapon. These have a Strength of 1 and a range of 8", and the Hero may re-roll any failed To Wound Rolls when using stones as a Throwing Weapon.

keywords.name: Orcish Brawler
keywords.definition: If this Hero is outnumbered during a Fight then they gain a bonus of +1 to their Attacks value for the duration of the Combat.

keywords.name: Animosity
keywords.definition: If the Hero is an Orc, they gain a bonus of +1 To Wound whilst a friendly Uruk-hai is engaged in the same combat. If the Hero is an Uruk-hai, they gain a bonus of +1 To Wound whilst a friendly Orc is engaged in the same combat.

keywords.name: She Hungers for Sweeter Meats
keywords.definition: This Hero adds 1 to their Attacks characteristic whilst they are Engaged in Combat with an enemy Man, Elf, Dwarf or Hobbit model.

keywords.name: Morgul Weaponry
keywords.definition: Each time this Hero inflicts an unsaved Wound on an enemy model, roll a D6. On a 5+, that model suffers an additional Wound (Fate may still be used as normal).

keywords.name: Show of Strength
keywords.definition: If this Hero slays one or more enemy models in Combat, then for the duration of the following turn they gain a bonus of +1 to their Fight Value.

keywords.name: Pillager
keywords.definition: The Hero gains +1 to Wound when making Strikes whilst within 3" of an Objective Marker, static or otherwise.

keywords.name: There will be no dawn for Men
keywords.definition: The Hero gains the Hatred (Man) special rule.

keywords.name: Savage Charge
keywords.definition: The Hero still gains the Extra Attack bonus even when they Charge a Cavalry model, and will retain it even if they are subsequently Charged by a Cavalry model.

keywords.name: Feral Charge
keywords.definition: When the Hero Charges an enemy Infantry model, they gain the Knock to the Ground bonus as if they were Cavalry. This bonus is lost if they are subsequently Charged by an enemy Cavalry model.

keywords.name: Whipped into a Frenzy
keywords.definition: Whenever this Hero suffers a Wound, roll a D6. On the roll of a natural 6, the Wound is ignored. If this Hero would later gain a special rule with the same effect (e.g. Oblivious to Pain) then treat that special rule as improving Whipped into a Frenzy to a natural 5+.

keywords.name: Strength in Numbers
keywords.definition: The Hero gains the Backstabbers special rule.

keywords.name: Callous Leadership
keywords.definition: At the start of the Fight Phase, before Heroic Actions are declared, the Hero may spend a Will Point to use this special rule. All friendly Goblin models within 3" gain a +1 To Wound when making Strikes. However, any friendly Goblin model within 3" that loses a Duel roll (including supporting models) must roll a D6 after any Strikes have been made. On a 1, the model suffers a Wound.

keywords.name: Cover of Darkness
keywords.definition: As part of this Hero's activation, they may spend a Will point and declare they are using this ability. Until the End Phase, the Fighting at Night special rules will be in play. (see page 137 of the Middle- earth Strategy Battle Game Rules Manual)

keywords.name: Master of Poisons
keywords.definition: This Hero must re-roll all failed To Wound rolls.

keywords.name: Seize Command
keywords.definition: If during the End Phase of any turn your Leader has only a single Wound remaining and is within 3" and Line of Sight of this Hero, you may choose to remove your Leader as a casualty. If you do, this Hero immediately assumes the role of "Leader" for the purposes of Victory Points instead. Do not make an Injury roll for models removed in this way. This model cannot use this special rule on itself.

keywords.name: Skilled Blade
keywords.definition: When fighting an enemy Hero, this Hero may force their opponent to reroll one of their dice in the Duel roll. This is not cumulative with other special rules that confer the same effect.

keywords.name: Master Skirmisher
keywords.definition: The Hero may still fire a bow even if they have moved over half their Move value this turn. If the Hero fires a Blowpipe or a Throwing Weapon, they instead do not suffer the -1 penalty for moving. Additionally, the Hero does not suffer the -1 penalty for using a two-handed weapon in a turn in which they Charged.

keywords.name: Master Hunter
keywords.definition: This Hero does not suffer any penalties for Moving through Difficult Terrain. Additionally, they may still gain the bonuses for Charging whilst in Difficult Terrain if they have the Cavalry keyword.

keywords.name: Swap with Me!
keywords.definition: At the start of the Fight Phase, before the Declare Heroic Actions Step, the Hero can choose a friendly Goblin model on a 25mm base within 3"and swap places with it. This does not count as Moving.

keywords.name: Feel no Pain
keywords.definition: Whenever this Hero suffers a Wound, roll a D6. On the roll of a natural 5+, the Wound is ignored.

keywords.name: Command Support
keywords.definition: A keyword some equipment (a War Drum, a War Horn, a Pennant, an Instrument) gives its bearer to stand for the leader's command retinue. It has no effect in play: a few scenarios score Victory Points for Command Support models still alive at the end of the game.

keywords.name: Laden with Baggage
keywords.definition: A Baggage Pony has a carrying capacity of up to 15 pieces of Equipment, weapons or additional wargear (except mounts). Whilst these pieces are on the Packhorse, the company gains no benefit from them. During the War's Aftermath, after determining injuries but before determining the next scenario, any member of a Battle Company may retrieve, store, or swap one of its pieces of Wargear or Equipment for an item from the Pony. During a scenario, any member of a Battle Company that begins its turn in base contact with the Pony may do likewise. Note that your Battle Company must still abide by the Wargear Limits at all times and each member must follow restrictions for Warriors and Heroes as normal.

keywords.name: Keen Sight (Falcon)
keywords.definition: Enemy models within 12" of a Falcon that is separate from its Hero may not benefit from the Stalk Unseen special rule.
keywords.label: Keen Sight

keywords.name: Handler's Glove
keywords.definition: This Creature starts the game upon the arm of its master rather than on the board. At the start of any turn in which the Creature is on their Hero model's arm, the Hero may release the creature - place it anywhere within 3" of the Hero. Whilst separate from its Hero, the Creature may move independently. If, during the End phase of any turn, a Creature is within 3" of their Hero, it may choose to land back on their Hero model's arm. Remove the Creature from the board. Whilst upon the Hero model's arm, the Creature cannot be targeted, attacked or hit with shooting attacks, and will not provide an In The Way roll for their Hero.

keywords.name: Well-aimed Shot
keywords.definition: When making a shooting attack, the first time this model fails an In The Way Roll he may make an Intelligence Test. If the test is passed, the In The Way Roll will be successful instead.

keywords.name: A fell light is in them
keywords.definition:
At the end of this model's Move, it can choose a single enemy model within 12" and Line of Sight. The chosen model must take an Intelligence Test. If the test is failed, you may Move the chosen model up to its Move Value directly towards this model, even if it has already Moved that turn.
 The chosen model will stop Moving if it would enter the Control Zone of an enemy model (with the exception of this model), If it comes into contact with an Obstacle, another model (though they will never count as Charging in this instance, and therefore cannot be involved in Combat with the model) or piece of impassable terrain, or if the model reaches the edge of a cliff or other such edge that would cause it to take falling damage.
 This Move cannot be used to move a Model out of Combat, make a model dismount, drop an item, or Lie Down. However, if the Move would allow the chosen model to Charge this model, then this model may make them Charge. A model affected by this special rule cannot Move any further that turn, and may not use Active abilities.
keywords.source: Spelling used by the vanilla units; the vanilla rule is A Fell Light is in Them
keywords.overrides: A Fell Light is in Them

keywords.name: At Path's End
keywords.definition: This unit earns no Experience Points and cannot level up (no progression, no promotion, no Hero in the Making).

keywords.name: Whirl of Attacks
keywords.definition: When rolling a natural 6 for the Duel Roll, this model rolls an additional attack when rolling to Wound. You can not use this rule if the enemy model is trapped.

keywords.name: Master of Fighting Styles
keywords.definition: The Hero has mastered different fighting styles. Before the Duel Roll, the model may use the rules for a two-handed weapon or shielding, even without the equipment.

keywords.name: I shall pass!
keywords.definition: If this Hero wins his Duel Roll, after all models have backed away but before making Strikes, the model may make no Strikes and instead move again up to half its Move Value. If it charges an enemy, it fights as normal. This rule can only be used once per turn. (Inspired by the Barge Brutal Power attack.)

parameterisedRules.name: Hatred

parameter.name: X
parameter.description: A race, faction or nationality keyword. The rule works against enemy models with that keyword; any race may be chosen when the rule is taken.

parameterisedRules.definition: A model with this special rule gains a bonus of +1 To Wound when making Strikes against a model with the same keyword as the one shown in brackets. So, a model with the Hatred (Man) special rule would gain a bonus of +1 To Wound when making Strikes against Man models.

parameterisedRules.name: Poisoned Attacks

parameter.name: X
parameter.description: One of the weapons on the model's profile, chosen when the rule is taken (e.g. with Envenom Weapon (X)). Only that weapon benefits.

parameterisedRules.definition:
A model with this special rule most re-roll any To Wound Rolls of a natural 1 when making Shooting Attacks or making Strikes.
 Sometimes, a particular weapon will be described as benefiting from this special rule. When this is the case, only To Wound Roll made for that weapon will be able to re-roll To Wound Rolls of a natural 1.

parameterisedRules.name: Master of Battle

parameter.name: X
parameter.description: The D6 score needed, from 2+ (best) to 6+ (worst).

parameterisedRules.definition: Whenever an enemy Hero declares a Heroic Action within 6" of this model, this model may roll a D6. If the result on the dice equals or beats the number shown in brackets, then this model may Immediately declare a Heroic Action of the same type without spending a Might Point. This may still be done if this model has no Might Points remaining or would not normally be able to declare that Heroic Action. If the roll is failed, this model may still declare a Heroic Action if they wish (though not one they cannot usually declare) for the usual cost of a Might Point.

parameterisedRules.name: Dominant

parameter.name: X
parameter.description: How many models the model counts as.

parameterisedRules.definition:
This model counts as the number of models as shown in brackets when working out how many models are in range of an objective, in a specific are of the board, or when working out how many models have escaped the battlefield. So, a model with Dominant (3) would count as three models in range of an objective, or in a specific are of the board, or three models when working out how many models have excaped the battlefield. If a model would gain this special rule whilst in range of another model or specific area of the board, and then moves off the board, they will not gain the benefit of this special rule once off the board.
 If a model has two sources of the Dominant (X) special rule, then they use the highest value.

parameterisedRules.name: Fury

parameter.name: X
parameter.description: The species (keywords) of the friendly models that benefit; chosen when the power is taken, normally the company's race.

parameterisedRules.definition: This Magical Power targets the caster. Friendly models within 6" of the caster who have the same keywords as those shown in brackets will automatically pass any Courage Tests they are required to take.

parameterisedRules.name: Combat Synergy

parameter.name: X
parameter.description: A friendly Hero of the same Battle Company, selected when the rule is taken (vanilla names Kili and Fili).

parameterisedRules.definition: At the start of any phase, before the Declare Heroic Actions step, if this Hero and X are within 1" of each other then they can swap places with each other - this does not count as Moving. If they have used this special rule during a turn, then during the Fight Phase of that turn they may each re-roll a single D6 when making a Duel Roll.

parameterisedRules.name: Terror

parameter.name: X
parameter.description: Optional restriction: only models with this keyword are affected.

parameterisedRules.definition:
If a model wishes to Charge a model with this special rule, then it must take a Courage Test at the start of its Move. If the test is passed, the model may Charge as normal. If the test is failed, the model cannot Move that turn, but may otherwise act normally.
 Sometimes a situation may open up the chance for a model to Charge a model with Terror part way through their Move, such as moving a different model with magic or killing something in the way with a throwing weapon. In such instances, the model only needs to take the Courage Test at the point in which the Terror causing model becomes possible to Charge. If a model making a Jump, Climb or Leap Test finishes within the Control Zone of an enemy with Terror and would normally be able to Charge, they will take their Courage Test after they have made their Jump, Climb or Leap Test.
 Sometimes, a model may only cause Terror In certain enemies. In these Instances, a keyword will follow Terror in brackets, and only models with that keyword will need to take a Courage Test to Charge the model. So, a model with Terror (Orc) will only cause Terror In Orc models, When the rule is shown with a keyword in brackets (e.g. the Torching Brand's Terror (Beast) and Terror (Cavalry)), it only affects models that have that keyword.

scenarioDetails.name: Seize Ground
scenarioDetails.description: As two companies become locked in a battle of wits and cunning, it becomes apparent that victory can only be seized by claiming key areas of the battlefield. As both leaders rally their followers, a fight for control of the battlefield is about to begin.
scenarioDetails.armies: All available members of each Battle Company.
scenarioDetails.layout: Set up terrain as described on page 65. Then, place five Objective Markers on the battlefield; one is automatically placed in the centre of the board. To place the other objectives, both players roll a D6. The player with the highest score places one objective anywhere on the battlefield at least 12" away from the existing objective and 6" away from any board edge. Their opponent then places a third objective at least 12" away from existing objectives and at least 6" away from any board edge. The players then alternate placing the remaining two objectives, according to the restriction noted earlier.
scenarioDetails.startingPositions:
Both players roll a D6, with the highest scoring player choosing their table edge. They then select a model of their Battle Company, and any attached Creatures, to deploy wholly within 12" of their board edge. Creatures must be deployed within 6" of their owner.

When this has been done, the opposing player chooses one of their models and deploys it in similar fashion. Players then alternate until all models have been placed.
scenarioDetails.objectives: The game lasts until the end of a turn in which one Army has been reduced to a quarter (25%) of its starting number of models or below, at which point the player that has scored the most Victory Points wins the game. If both players have the same number of Victory Points, the game is a draw.

scoringObjectives.text: For each Objective Marker, you score 1 Victory Point if you have more models within 3" than your opponent. If you have at least twice as many models as your opponent within 3", you instead score 2 Victory Points. If you are the only player to have models within 3", you instead score 3 Victory Points.

If you have at least twice as many models as your opponent within 3", you instead score 2 Victory Points.
If you are the only player to have models within 3", you instead score 3 Victory Points.

scoringObjectives.text: You score 1 Victory Point if the enemy Battle Company is Broken at the end of the game. If the enemy Battle Company is Broken and your Battle Company is not, you instead score 3 Victory Points.

options.text: You score 1 Victory Point if the enemy Battle Company is Broken at the end of the game.
If the enemy Battle Company is Broken and your Battle Company is not, you instead score 3 Victory Points.

scenarioDetails.name: Chance Encounter
scenarioDetails.description: Upon their travels through Middle-earth, two opposing Battle Companies have happened upon each other. A company that is seemingly alone, and with no support in sight, is not an opportunity to pass up lightly. As the companies engage, a solid tactical mind and skill at arms will see victory won.
scenarioDetails.armies: All available members of each Battle Company.
scenarioDetails.layout: Set up terrain as described on page 65.
scenarioDetails.startingPositions:
Both players roll a D6, with the highest scoring player choosing their table edge. They then select a model of their Battle Company, and any attached Creatures, to deploy wholly within 12" of their board edge. Creatures must be deployed within 6" of their owner.

When this has been done, the opposing player chooses one of their models and deploys it in similar fashion. Players then alternate until all models have been placed.
scenarioDetails.objectives: The game lasts until the end of a turn in which one Battle Company has been reduced to 25% of its starting models, at which point the player who has scored the most Victory Points wins the game. If both players have the same number of Victory Points, the game is a draw.

scoringObjectives.text: You score 1 Victory Point if the enemy Leader was wounded during the game. If the enemy Leader has been wounded, and only has 1 Wound remaining, then you instead score 3 Victory Points. If the enemy Leader was removed as a casualty, you instead score 5 Victory Points.

options.text: You score 1 Victory Point if the enemy Leader was wounded during the game.
If the enemy Leader has been wounded, and only has 1 Wound remaining, then you instead score 3 Victory Points.
If the enemy Leader was removed as a casualty, you instead score 5 Victory Points.

scoringObjectives.text: You score 3 Victory Points if the enemy Battle Company is Broken at the end of the game. If the enemy Battle Company is Broken and your Battle Company is not, you instead score 5 Victory Points.

options.text: You score 3 Victory Points if the enemy Battle Company is Broken at the end of the game.
If the enemy Battle Company is Broken and your Battle Company is not, you instead score 5 Victory Points.

scoringObjectives.text: You score 2 Victory Points if your opponent has no Company Support remaining at the end of the game.

options.text: You score 2 Victory Points if your opponent has no Company Support remaining at the end of the game.

scoringObjectives.text: You score 1 Victory Point if you have at least one Command Support remaining at the end of the game. If you have more Command Support alive than your opponent, then you instead score 2 Victory Points.

options.text: You score 1 Victory Point if you have at least one Command Support remaining at the end of the game.
If you have more Command Support alive than your opponent, then you instead score 2 Victory Points.

scoringObjectives.text: You score 3 Victory Points if the enemy Battle Company has been reduced to 25% of its starting models at the end of the game.

options.text: You score 3 Victory Points if the enemy Battle Company has been reduced to 25% of its starting models at the end of the game.

rewards.name: Rendezvous
rewards.text: The victorious Battle Company may apply +1 / -1 to their first Reinforcement roll in the subsequent War's Aftermath.

scoring: You score 1 Victory Point if the enemy Leader was wounded during the game. If the enemy Leader has been wounded, and only has 1 Wound remaining, then you instead score 3 Victory Points. If the enemy Leader was removed as a casualty, you instead score 5 Victory Points.
You score 3 Victory Points if the enemy Battle Company is Broken at the end of the game. If the enemy Battle Company is Broken and your Battle Company is not, you instead score 5 Victory Points.
You score 2 Victory Points if your opponent has no Company Support remaining at the end of the game.

You score 1 Victory Point if you have at least one Command Support remaining at the end of the game. If you have more Command Support alive than your opponent, then you instead score 2 Victory Points.
You score 3 Victory Points if the enemy Battle Company has been reduced to 25% of its starting models at the end of the game.
You score 1 Victory Point for each enemy Hero model that has been removed as a casualty, up to a maximum of 3 Victory Points.

scenarioDetails.name: Secure the Area
scenarioDetails.description: Hidden somewhere upon the battlefield lies something of great value to both sides. Whether this is a hoard of treasure, the entrance to a secret passageway, the fallen body of an ally or even something much more valuable; both sides must strive to claim it and defend it at all costs.
scenarioDetails.armies: All available members of each Battle Company.
scenarioDetails.layout: Set up terrain as described on page 65. Once the battlefield has been set up, an Objective Marker is placed in the centre of the battlefield. Players must also agree which direction is north – this is important for determining where and when Reinforcements arrive from.
scenarioDetails.startingPositions: At the battle's start, the Battle Companies are yet to arrive – models are not deployed at the start of the game, but will enter as the game continues (see Maelstrom of Battle).
scenarioDetails.objectives:
Once one Battle Company has been Broken, the game might suddenly end. At the end of each turn after this condition has been met, roll a D6. On the result of 1-2, the game ends – otherwise, the battle continues for another turn!

At the end of the game, the player who has scored the most Victory Points wins the game. If both players have the same number of Victory Points, the game is a draw.

scenarioDetails.name: Tame the Beast
scenarioDetails.description: Somewhere in the wilderness, a lone Troll is causing havoc, smashing its way through nearby settlements and leaving devastation in its wake. The Troll poses an immediate threat to two rival Battle Companies, both of who need it to be brought down. As the two companies track the Troll, they spy each other in the distance. Hunting the Troll has now become a show of dominance as well as a necessity.
scenarioDetails.armies:
All available members of each Battle Company.

1 Cave Troll or Hill Troll
scenarioDetails.layout: Set up terrain as described on page 65.
scenarioDetails.startingPositions: The Monsters are placed in the centre of the board. Both players roll a D6, with the highest scoring player choosing their table edge. They then place their Battle Company within 12" of their chosen edge. Their opponent then places their Battle Company within 12" of the opposite board edge.
scenarioDetails.objectives:
Both companies have made it their mission to slay the Troll and bring back its head as proof, whichever is successful will vastly increase its status within the ranks of their army.

Once the Monster(s) has been slain, the game may suddenly end. At the end of each turn after this condition has been met, roll a D6. On a 1-2 the game ends, otherwise it continues for another turn.
